# Data dictionary

This document describes every field, dimension code, Zetaris column, and decode rule used by the Eurostat
`une_rt_m` registration. It is intentionally exhaustive: the source is a sparse JSON-stat object, and most
implementation mistakes come from treating its dynamic-key objects as arrays or maps without checking the
shape.

## Source JSON-stat fields

The live PL/T response has 11 top-level fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `version` | string | JSON-stat version. Observed `2.0`. |
| `class` | string | Object class. Observed `dataset`. |
| `label` | string | Dataset title: "Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data". |
| `source` | string | Source agency. Observed `ESTAT`. |
| `updated` | string | Source update timestamp, `2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200`. |
| `value` | object of string to number | Sparse observations. Keys are stringified flat indices; values are rates or levels. |
| `status` | object of string to string | Optional observation status flags. Keys are stringified flat indices; values are codes such as `b`, `d`, `p`, `u`. |
| `id` | array of string | Dimension order: `freq`, `s_adj`, `age`, `unit`, `sex`, `geo`, `time`. |
| `size` | array of number | Dimension cardinalities. Full dataset: `[1, 3, 3, 2, 3, 38, 525]`. |
| `dimension` | object of string to dimension | Per-dimension category index and labels. |
| `extension` | object | Structural metadata, annotations, no-data positions, and status labels. |

### `dimension` object

Each entry under `dimension` has this shape:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `label` | string | Human-readable dimension name, such as "Time frequency". |
| `category` | object | Category metadata. |
| `category.index` | object of string to number | Maps a category code or period label to its integer position. |
| `category.label` | object of string to string | Maps a category code or period label to a human-readable label. |

For the time dimension, `category.index` maps a period such as `2026-08` to an integer. The key is already
human-readable, so decoding time does not require `category.label`.

### `extension` object

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `extension.agencyId` | string | `ESTAT`. |
| `extension.id` | string | `UNE_RT_M`. |
| `extension.version` | string | `1.0` for the extension payload. |
| `extension.lang` | string | `EN`. |
| `extension.datastructure` | object | `{id: "UNE_RT_M", agencyId: "ESTAT", version: "156.0"}`. |
| `extension.annotation` | array | 19 annotation objects. Includes DOI, explanatory links, ESMS links, observation count, period bounds, and update timestamps. |
| `extension.positions-with-no-data` | object | Per-dimension arrays of positions with no data. For the PL slice, only `time` is non-empty: 169 indices. |
| `extension.status.label` | object of string to string | Maps status codes to labels. Observed `b`, `d`, `p`, `u`. |

The annotation types observed in the PL/T response are:

| Annotation type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `CREATED` | Dataset creation timestamp. |
| `DISSEMINATION_DOI_XML` | DOI identifier payload. |
| `DISSEMINATION_EXPLANATORY_LINK` | Link to the information note PDF. |
| `DISSEMINATION_OBJECT_TYPE` | `DATASET`. |
| `DISSEMINATION_TIMESTAMP_DATA` | Data update timestamp. |
| `DISSEMINATION_TIMESTAMP_GLOBAL` | Global update timestamp. |
| `DISSEMINATION_TIMESTAMP_PLANNED` | Planned update timestamp. |
| `ESMS_HTML` | ESMS metadata page. |
| `ESMS_SDMX` | ESMS SDMX download. |
| `FOOTNOTE` | Footnote workbook. |
| `OBS_COUNT` | `757828` for the full dataset. |
| `OBS_PERIOD_OVERALL_LATEST` | `2026-09`. |
| `OBS_PERIOD_OVERALL_OLDEST` | `1983-01`. |
| `SOURCE_INSTITUTIONS` | `Eurostat`. |
| `UPDATE_DATA` | Data update timestamp. |
| `UPDATE_FOOTNOTES` | Footnote update timestamp. |
| `UPDATE_STRUCTURE` | Structure update timestamp. |

## Dimension codes

### Fixed dimensions

| Dimension | Full codes | Registered slice | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `freq` | `M` | `M` | Monthly only. |
| `s_adj` | `NSA`, `SA`, `TC` | `SA` | The registered slice is seasonally adjusted, not calendar adjusted. |
| `age` | `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, `Y25-74` | `TOTAL` | `Y_LT25` is under 25; `Y25-74` is 25 to 74. |
| `unit` | `THS_PER`, `PC_ACT` | `PC_ACT` | `THS_PER` is thousands of persons; `PC_ACT` is a percentage of the labour force. |
| `sex` | `T`, `M`, `F` | `T` | Total, males, females. |
| `geo` | 38 categories | `PL` | See the full table below. |
| `time` | 525 months | 525 months | `1983-01` to `2026-09`. |

### Geography codes

The following table lists every `geo` category in the full dataset. The counts and ranges are for the fixed
slice `sex=T`, `age=TOTAL`, `unit=PC_ACT`, `s_adj=SA`. They are useful for choosing additional registrations
without re-querying the API.

| Code | Label | Values | First | Last | Missing |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: |
| `EU27_2020` | European Union - 27 countries (from 2020) | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `EA21` | Euro area - 21 countries (from 2026) | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `BE` | Belgium | 485 | 1986-04 | 2026-08 | 40 |
| `BG` | Bulgaria | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `CZ` | Czechia | 404 | 1993-01 | 2026-08 | 121 |
| `DK` | Denmark | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |
| `DE` | Germany | 428 | 1991-01 | 2026-08 | 97 |
| `EE` | Estonia | 319 | 2000-02 | 2026-08 | 206 |
| `IE` | Ireland | 525 | 1983-01 | 2026-09 | 0 |
| `EL` | Greece | 341 | 1998-04 | 2026-08 | 184 |
| `ES` | Spain | 485 | 1986-04 | 2026-08 | 40 |
| `FR` | France | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |
| `HR` | Croatia | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `IT` | Italy | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |
| `CY` | Cyprus | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `LV` | Latvia | 341 | 1998-04 | 2026-08 | 184 |
| `LT` | Lithuania | 344 | 1998-01 | 2026-08 | 181 |
| `LU` | Luxembourg | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |
| `HU` | Hungary | 368 | 1996-01 | 2026-08 | 157 |
| `MT` | Malta | 320 | 2000-01 | 2026-08 | 205 |
| `NL` | Netherlands | 525 | 1983-01 | 2026-09 | 0 |
| `AT` | Austria | 380 | 1995-01 | 2026-08 | 145 |
| `PL` | Poland | 356 | 1997-01 | 2026-08 | 169 |
| `PT` | Portugal | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |
| `RO` | Romania | 356 | 1997-01 | 2026-08 | 169 |
| `SI` | Slovenia | 368 | 1996-01 | 2026-08 | 157 |
| `SK` | Slovakia | 344 | 1998-01 | 2026-08 | 181 |
| `FI` | Finland | 465 | 1988-01 | 2026-09 | 60 |
| `SE` | Sweden | 525 | 1983-01 | 2026-09 | 0 |
| `IS` | Iceland | 284 | 2003-01 | 2026-08 | 241 |
| `NO` | Norway | 452 | 1989-01 | 2026-08 | 73 |
| `CH` | Switzerland | 198 | 2010-01 | 2026-06 | 327 |
| `UK` | United Kingdom | 453 | 1983-01 | 2020-09 | 72 |
| `BA` | Bosnia and Herzegovina | 67 | 2021-01 | 2026-07 | 458 |
| `MK` | North Macedonia | 248 | 2006-01 | 2026-08 | 277 |
| `TR` | Türkiye | 259 | 2005-01 | 2026-07 | 266 |
| `US` | United States | 523 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 2 |
| `JP` | Japan | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 |

`Missing` is `525` minus the number of populated values. It includes leading months before a country's series
starts, the empty latest month, and any country-specific gaps. The full dataset does not report a global
`positions-with-no-data.time` list; absence from `value` is the signal.

## Zetaris object map

| Object | Type | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `EUROSTAT_REST` | Lightning database (id 917) | Registration container for the Eurostat REST source. |
| `eurostat` | Schemastore container | Holds the decoded views. |
| `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` | REST table | Raw JSON-stat response for the fixed PL slice. |
| `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table` | View | Dataset label, source, update timestamp, geo labels, and time index map. |
| `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table` | View | Three fixed rate columns for a low-risk spot check. |
| `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table` | View | Fully decoded `(period, rate)` rows. |

## REST table fields

`EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` has 11 top-level fields.

| Field | Shape | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `class` | string | `dataset`. |
| `dimension` | struct | Nested dimension metadata. Contains `freq`, `s_adj`, `age`, `unit`, `sex`, `geo`, `time`. |
| `extension` | struct | Annotations, data structure, no-data positions, and status labels. |
| `id` | array of string | Dimension order. |
| `label` | string | Dataset title. |
| `size` | array of number | Dimension sizes for the fixed slice: `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 525]`. |
| `source` | string | `ESTAT`. |
| `status` | struct | Dynamic-key status flags for two PL months. |
| `updated` | string | Source timestamp. |
| `value` | struct | Dynamic-key values for 356 months. |
| `version` | string | `2.0`. |

The dynamic-key fields are inferred as structs, not maps. `value` has one field per populated flat index;
`dimension.time.category.index` has one field per time category. This is the reason the decode view applies
`from_json(to_json(...))` before `explode()`.

## Metadata view

`eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table` has five columns.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dataset_label` | string | "Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data". |
| `dataset_source` | string | `ESTAT`. |
| `last_updated` | string | `2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200`. |
| `geo_labels` | `struct<PL:string>` | `{"PL":"Poland"}`. |
| `time_index_map` | struct with 525 `bigint` fields | Maps every period label, including `2026-09`, to its integer index. |

`time_index_map` is a struct, not a map. It is convenient for a human or for a direct backtick access such as
`time_index_map.\`2026-09\``, but it is not directly `explode()`-able without the same JSON coercion used for
`value`.

## Snapshot view

`eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table` has exactly three columns.

| Column | Type | Period | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | ---: |
| `rate_1997_01` | double | 1997-01 | 11.8 |
| `rate_2025_07` | double | 2025-07 | 3.1 |
| `rate_2026_07` | double | 2026-07 | 3.4 |

The view is a spot check. It is not a wide-format table and it does not include `2026-08`, even though the
series view does. The column names encode the period, so adding a month requires a schema change.

## Series view

`eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table` has two columns.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `period` | string | Calendar month in `YYYY-MM` form. |
| `unemployment_rate_pct` | double | Unemployment rate as a percentage of the labour force. |

The view has 356 rows, one per populated month, from `1997-01` to `2026-08`. It does not carry status flags.
If a consumer needs the flags, it must read the raw `status` struct from `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` or the API.

## Missing and status semantics

### Missing values

There are two different signals:

1. **`extension.positions-with-no-data`** is an explicit list of positions that the source declares as having
   no data. For the PL slice, `time` has 169 positions: `0` through `167` and `524`. The other dimensions have
   empty arrays.
2. **Absence from `value`** is the general signal. The full dataset has no global `positions-with-no-data.time`
   list, so a missing flat index is simply not present in `value`.

Do not infer missingness from a zero or an empty string. The source uses absent keys, not sentinel values.

### Status codes

| Code | Label | Full-dataset count | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `b` | break in time series | 1,307 | The series has a break at this observation. |
| `d` | definition differs (see metadata) | 846 | The definition differs from the standard; consult metadata. |
| `p` | provisional | 5,832 | The value is provisional and may be revised. |
| `u` | low reliability | 3,306 | The value has low reliability. |

The top-level `status` object is keyed by the same flat index as `value`. The `extension.status.label` object
maps the codes to their labels; it does not carry per-observation flags.

### Status flags in the five-country comparison

| Country | Flagged months | Codes |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| Poland | 2 | `2009-01` = b; `2009-12` = d |
| Germany | 2 | `2005-03` = d; `2009-01` = b |
| France | 3 | `1995-12` = d; `2003-01` = b; `2021-01` = d |
| Spain | 1 | `1995-12` = d |
| Italy | 109 | `1983-01`–`1991-12` = p (108 months); `2004-01` = b |

The flags are attached to the observations. The Zetaris series view drops them, so a SQL consumer that needs
to exclude provisional or low-reliability values must join back to the raw REST table.

## Decode technique

### Flat index

JSON-stat stores observations in a flat array (or, here, a sparse object keyed by the flat index). The flat
index is:

```text
flat = sum(index[d] * stride[d])
stride[d] = product(size[d + 1 :])
```

For the registered PL slice, every dimension except `time` has size 1, so the flat index equals the time
index. `2026-08` has time index `523`, so its flat index is `523`.

For the full dataset, the stride vector is:

```text
[1077300, 359100, 119700, 59850, 19950, 525, 1]
```

For the full-dataset cell `freq=M`, `s_adj=SA`, `age=TOTAL`, `unit=PC_ACT`, `sex=T`, `geo=PL`,
`time=2026-08`, the indices are `0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 22, 523`, and the flat index is:

```text
1*359100 + 1*59850 + 22*525 + 523 = 431023
```

### SQL decode

The registered series view uses two coercions and an equality join:

```sql
SELECT
    time_label AS period,
    CAST(rate_value AS DOUBLE) AS unemployment_rate_pct
FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl
LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(value), 'map<string,double>')) AS time_key, rate_value
LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(dimension.time.category.index), 'map<string,bigint>')) AS time_label, time_index_value
WHERE CAST(time_key AS INT) = time_index_value;
```

Both `value` and `dimension.time.category.index` must be coerced. A plain `explode()` on either field fails
with a `DATATYPE_MISMATCH` because both are inferred as structs, not maps. The join compares the stringified
flat index in `value` with the integer time index.

### Python decode

A minimal, dependency-free decoder for the registered slice:

```python
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen

URL = (
    "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m"
    "?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA"
)

with urlopen(URL, timeout=60) as response:
    dataset = json.load(response)

time_index = dataset["dimension"]["time"]["category"]["index"]
index_to_period = {position: period for period, position in time_index.items()}
rows = sorted(
    (index_to_period[int(key)], value)
    for key, value in dataset["value"].items()
)
for period, value in rows[-3:]:
    print(period, value)
```

The decoder assumes the filtered slice has size 1 on every non-time dimension. For a multi-dimension slice,
compute the flat index with the stride formula instead of treating the `value` key as a time index.

## Example rows

### Metadata view

```text
dataset_label: Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data
dataset_source: ESTAT
last_updated: 2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200
geo_labels: {"PL":"Poland"}
```

### Snapshot view

```text
rate_1997_01: 11.8
rate_2025_07: 3.1
rate_2026_07: 3.4
```

### Series view

| `period` | `unemployment_rate_pct` | Note |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `1997-01` | 11.8 | First populated month. |
| `2009-01` | 7.4 | Status `b` in the raw source. |
| `2009-12` | 9.1 | Status `d` in the raw source. |
| `2026-08` | 3.4 | Latest populated month. |

# Eurostat Statistics API reference

## Endpoint

| Property | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Base URL | `https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/` |
| Dataset path | `une_rt_m` |
| Method | `GET` |
| Authentication | None |
| Registration | None |
| Response format | JSON-stat 2.0 when `format=JSON` |
| CORS | Enabled (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) |
| Typical content type | `application/json` |

The canonical request for the registered Zetaris slice is:

```text
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Values used here | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `format` | Recommended | `JSON` | Return JSON-stat instead of SDMX or another format. |
| `lang` | Recommended | `EN` | Language for labels and metadata. |
| `freq` | Optional | `M` | Monthly frequency. The dataset contains only `M`. |
| `s_adj` | Optional | `SA` | Seasonal adjustment. Full codes: `NSA`, `SA`, `TC`. |
| `age` | Optional | `TOTAL` | Age class. Full codes: `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, `Y25-74`. |
| `unit` | Optional | `PC_ACT` | Unit. Full codes: `THS_PER`, `PC_ACT`. |
| `sex` | Optional | `T` | Sex. Full codes: `T`, `M`, `F`. |
| `geo` | Optional | `PL` | Geography. Full dataset has 38 categories. |
| `time` | Optional | Omitted | Time filter. The registration returns the full 525-month axis. |

Omitting a dimension returns all of its categories. The API does not require every dimension to be filtered.
The registered Zetaris slice fixes six dimensions and leaves `time` unfiltered.

### Fixed dimensions in the registration

| Dimension | Value | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `freq` | `M` | The dataset is monthly. |
| `s_adj` | `SA` | The registration uses the headline seasonally adjusted series. |
| `age` | `TOTAL` | The registration uses the total age class. |
| `unit` | `PC_ACT` | The registration uses rates, not levels. |
| `sex` | `T` | The registration uses the total sex. |
| `geo` | `PL` | The registration is a Poland example. |

## Exact request URLs

### Registered slice

```text
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA
```

### Browser template

```text
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=M&s_adj=SA&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&sex={sex}&geo={geo}
```

Replace `{sex}` with `T`, `M`, or `F`, and `{geo}` with a supported country code such as `PL`, `DE`, `FR`,
`ES`, or `IT`.

### Full dataset

```text
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN
```

The full response is about 10 MB uncompressed at the time of verification. It is useful for exploration but
too large for a browser page that only needs one series.

## Response shape

A filtered response has 11 top-level fields:

```text
version, class, label, source, updated, value, status, id, size, dimension, extension
```

### Top-level fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `version` | string | `2.0`. |
| `class` | string | `dataset`. |
| `label` | string | Dataset title. |
| `source` | string | `ESTAT`. |
| `updated` | string | Source timestamp. |
| `value` | object | Sparse observations keyed by stringified flat index. |
| `status` | object | Optional status flags keyed by the same flat index. |
| `id` | array | Dimension order. |
| `size` | array | Dimension cardinalities. |
| `dimension` | object | Category indexes and labels per dimension. |
| `extension` | object | Annotations, no-data positions, and status labels. |

### Filtered slice dimensions

For the PL/T request, `id` and `size` are:

```text
id:   ["freq", "s_adj", "age", "unit", "sex", "geo", "time"]
size: [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 525]
```

The time axis has 525 categories, but only 356 have values. `value` is sparse; it does not contain keys for
the 169 empty positions.

### Response excerpt

```text
{
  "version": "2.0",
  "class": "dataset",
  "label": "Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data",
  "source": "ESTAT",
  "updated": "2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200",
  "value": {
    "168": 11.8,
    "169": 11.5,
    ...
    "523": 3.4
  },
  "status": {
    "312": "b",
    "323": "d"
  },
  "id": ["freq", "s_adj", "age", "unit", "sex", "geo", "time"],
  "size": [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 525],
  "dimension": {
    "time": {
      "label": "Time",
      "category": {
        "index": {
          "1983-01": 0,
          ...
          "1997-01": 168,
          ...
          "2026-08": 523,
          "2026-09": 524
        },
        "label": {
          "1983-01": "1983-01",
          ...
        }
      }
    },
    ...
  },
  "extension": {
    "datastructure": {
      "id": "UNE_RT_M",
      "agencyId": "ESTAT",
      "version": "156.0"
    },
    "positions-with-no-data": {
      "time": [0, 1, ..., 167, 524]
    },
    "status": {
      "label": {
        "b": "break in time series",
        "d": "definition differs (see metadata)"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The excerpt is illustrative; the real `value` object has 356 entries and the real `dimension.time.category.index`
has 525 entries.

## JSON-stat decoding

### Algorithm

1. Read `id` and `size`.
2. Build `stride[d] = product(size[d + 1:])`.
3. Invert `dimension.time.category.index` so the integer position maps to a period label.
4. For each time position, compute the flat index with the other dimensions fixed at index `0`:

   ```text
   flat = time_position * stride[time_dimension]
   ```

   This is valid for a request that filters every non-time dimension to one category. The registered slice
   does exactly that.
5. Read `value[String(flat)]`.
6. Keep only finite numeric values.
7. Sort ascending by period label.

For the registered slice, every non-time dimension has size 1, so the flat index equals the time position.
`2026-08` has position `523`, so its value is `value["523"]`.

### TypeScript decoder for a filtered request

```ts
export interface JsonStatDataset {
  version: string;
  class: "dataset";
  label: string;
  source: string;
  updated: string;
  value: Record<string, number>;
  status?: Record<string, string>;
  id: string[];
  size: number[];
  dimension: Record<string, {
    label: string;
    category: {
      index: Record<string, number>;
      label: Record<string, string>;
    };
  }>;
  extension?: {
    status?: { label?: Record<string, string> };
    "positions-with-no-data"?: { time?: number[] };
  };
}

export interface Observation {
  period: string;
  rate: number;
}

export function decodeSeries(dataset: JsonStatDataset): Observation[] {
  const timeDimension = dataset.id.indexOf("time");
  if (timeDimension === -1) {
    throw new Error("JSON-stat response has no time dimension");
  }

  const strides = dataset.size.map((_, index) =>
    dataset.size.slice(index + 1).reduce((product, size) => product * size, 1),
  );
  const timeIndex = dataset.dimension.time.category.index;
  const observations: Observation[] = [];

  for (const [period, position] of Object.entries(timeIndex)) {
    const flat = position * strides[timeDimension];
    const value = dataset.value[String(flat)];
    if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) {
      observations.push({ period, rate: value });
    }
  }

  return observations.sort((left, right) => left.period.localeCompare(right.period));
}
```

### Python decoder for a filtered request

```python
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen

URL = (
    "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m"
    "?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA"
)

with urlopen(URL, timeout=60) as response:
    dataset = json.load(response)

time_index = dataset["dimension"]["time"]["category"]["index"]
index_to_period = {position: period for period, position in time_index.items()}
rows = sorted(
    (index_to_period[int(key)], value)
    for key, value in dataset["value"].items()
)
print(rows[0], rows[-1])
```

### General flat-index decoder

For a response with more than one non-time category, compute the flat index with the full formula:

```text
flat = sum(category_index[d] * stride[d] for d in dimensions)
```

Do not assume that the `value` key is a time index unless every other dimension has size 1.

## Invalid codes

Eurostat does **not** return an HTTP error for an invalid dimension code. It returns HTTP 200 with an empty
category and an empty value object. Verified examples:

| Request | Observed |
| :--- | :--- |
| `age=Y15-74` | `dimension.age.category.index = {}`; `value = {}` |
| `geo=XX` | `dimension.geo.category.index = {}`; `value = {}` |

This looks like "no data available" rather than "wrong parameter". Validate codes against the allowlists before
requesting. The valid age codes are `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, and `Y25-74`; `Y15-74` is not valid for this dataset.

## Errors, CORS, and limits

### HTTP and network errors

- A malformed URL or unsupported format can return a 4xx response.
- A server-side problem can return a 5xx response.
- A network failure or a CORS change appears as a browser fetch rejection, not as a JSON error.
- The API does not use an API key, so there is no 401 path for this source.

### CORS

The live response includes:

```text
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Accept, X-Requested-With
```

This permits direct browser requests. If Eurostat changes the CORS policy, a browser client needs a proxy or
a server-side component. The repository's registered Zetaris table is not a browser proxy.

### Rate limits and caching

The source is public and does not publish a numeric rate limit in the response. Treat it as a shared public
service:

- Request one series at a time.
- Cache responses for a short period, such as five minutes.
- Do not loop over all 38 countries and 3 sex codes on every page load.
- Do not fetch the full 10 MB dataset for a single-series view.

The full dataset is 757,828 values and is not appropriate for a browser page that needs one country/sex pair.

## Data freshness and revisions

- `updated` is the authoritative source timestamp for the current vintage.
- The latest PL month is `2026-08`; `2026-09` is present but empty.
- Eurostat publishes monthly data approximately 31 days after the reference month.
- Routine revisions, annual seasonal-adjustment reviews, and major revisions can change historical values.
- The API does not expose a vintage history. Store the `updated` value alongside any derived artifact if
  reproducibility matters.

## References

- [Eurostat API Statistics guide](https://wikis.ec.europa.eu/display/EUROSTATHELP/API+Statistics+-+data+query)
- [JSON-stat specification](https://json-stat.org/)
- [Eurostat ESMS metadata for `une_rt_m`](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/en/une_rt_m_esms.htm)
- [Eurostat copyright notice](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice)
- [Dataset DOI](https://doi.org/10.2908/UNE_RT_M)

# Zetaris integration

This document describes the Eurostat registration that already exists in the Zetaris instance. It is a
single-country slice of `une_rt_m`, not a general Eurostat connector. The raw REST table is backed by the
public endpoint; the three views decode or expose parts of the JSON-stat response.

## Object inventory

| Object | Type | Identifier | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Eurostat database | Lightning database | `EUROSTAT_REST` (id 917) | Registration container. |
| Eurostat container | Schemastore container | `eurostat` | Holds the decoded views. |
| Raw slice | REST table | `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` | JSON-stat response for Poland, total sex, total age, `PC_ACT`, `SA`. |
| Metadata view | Schemastore view | `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table` | Dataset label, source, update timestamp, geo labels, time index map. |
| Snapshot view | Schemastore view | `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table` | Three fixed rate columns. |
| Series view | Schemastore view | `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table` | One `(period, rate)` row per populated month. |

The raw table name is written as `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` in the registration and referenced as
`eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl` in the view definitions. Zetaris identifiers are case-insensitive in these
examples; use the casing shown in the object inventory when writing new SQL.

## Registration request

The source is registered with `CREATE LIGHTNING REST TABLE`. The exact request block from
[`07_eurostat_create.sql`](../../../open_data/rest_apis/sql/non_rate_limited/07_eurostat_create.sql) is:

```sql
CREATE LIGHTNING REST TABLE une_rt_m_pl FROM EUROSTAT_REST REQUEST(
    endpoint "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA&lang=EN",
    method "get",
    response_type "json",
    http_encoding "URLENCODED"
) HEADER (
) BODY ();
```

The request has no headers and no body. The endpoint fixes the slice; there are no runtime parameters. To
register a different country or sex, create a separate REST table with a different URL and table name.

The database and container are created first:

```sql
CREATE LIGHTNING DATABASE EUROSTAT_REST DESCRIBE BY "Eurostat REST API JSON-stat source";
CREATE SCHEMASTORE CONTAINER eurostat;
```

## View definitions

### Metadata view

```sql
CREATE SCHEMASTORE VIEW une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table WITH CONTAINER eurostat AS
SELECT
    label AS dataset_label,
    source AS dataset_source,
    updated AS last_updated,
    dimension.geo.category.label AS geo_labels,
    dimension.time.category.index AS time_index_map
FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl;
```

This view is safe to query without `explode()`. It returns one row with:

| Column | Type | Observed value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dataset_label` | string | `Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data` |
| `dataset_source` | string | `ESTAT` |
| `last_updated` | string | `2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200` |
| `geo_labels` | `struct<PL:string>` | `{"PL":"Poland"}` |
| `time_index_map` | struct with 525 `bigint` fields | Period-to-index map, including `2026-09` |

`time_index_map` is a struct, not a map. It is convenient for direct backtick access, but it is not directly
`explode()`-able without JSON coercion.

### Snapshot view

```sql
CREATE SCHEMASTORE VIEW une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table WITH CONTAINER eurostat AS
SELECT
    value.`168` AS rate_1997_01,
    value.`510` AS rate_2025_07,
    value.`522` AS rate_2026_07
FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl;
```

The view has exactly three columns. It is a spot check, not a wide-format snapshot. The indices are:

| Column | Flat index | Period | Observed value |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | ---: |
| `rate_1997_01` | 168 | 1997-01 | 11.8 |
| `rate_2025_07` | 510 | 2025-07 | 3.1 |
| `rate_2026_07` | 522 | 2026-07 | 3.4 |

The series view includes `2026-08`, but the snapshot view does not. Do not use the snapshot view as the
latest-value source.

### Series view

```sql
CREATE SCHEMASTORE VIEW une_rt_m_pl_series_table WITH CONTAINER eurostat AS
SELECT
    time_label AS period,
    CAST(rate_value AS DOUBLE) AS unemployment_rate_pct
FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl
LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(value), 'map<string,double>')) AS time_key, rate_value
LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(dimension.time.category.index), 'map<string,bigint>')) AS time_label, time_index_value
WHERE CAST(time_key AS INT) = time_index_value;
```

Both dynamic-key objects are coerced with `from_json(to_json(...))`. A plain `explode()` fails because
Zetaris infers both objects as structs, not maps. The join compares the stringified flat index in `value`
with the integer time index.

The view has two columns:

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `period` | string | Calendar month in `YYYY-MM` form. |
| `unemployment_rate_pct` | double | Unemployment rate as a percentage of the labour force. |

It has 356 rows, one per populated month. It does not carry the source status flags.

## Verified state

Observed on 2026-10-23 against the live Zetaris instance:

| Check | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` selected fields | `class=dataset`, `source=ESTAT`, `updated=2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200`, `version=2.0` |
| Metadata row | Label, source, timestamp, and `geo_labels` as expected |
| Series row count | 356 |
| Series distinct periods | 356 |
| Series first period | `1997-01` |
| Series last period | `2026-08` |
| Snapshot values | `11.8`, `3.1`, `3.4` |
| Series view types | `period string`, `unemployment_rate_pct double` |
| Snapshot view types | `rate_1997_01 double`, `rate_2025_07 double`, `rate_2026_07 double` |
| Metadata view types | `dataset_label string`, `dataset_source string`, `last_updated string`, `geo_labels struct<PL:string>`, `time_index_map struct<...525 fields>` |

## Verification queries

Run the preflight first:

```bash
cd /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started
python3 scripts/preflight.py
```

Then run the checks one at a time:

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(period) AS first_period, MAX(period) AS last_period, COUNT(DISTINCT period) AS distinct_periods FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT period, unemployment_rate_pct FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table ORDER BY period DESC LIMIT 5"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT dataset_label, dataset_source, last_updated, geo_labels FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT rate_1997_01, rate_2025_07, rate_2026_07 FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "DESCRIBE eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "DESCRIBE eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table"
```

Expected outputs:

| Query | Expected |
| :--- | :--- |
| Count/range | `n=356`, `first_period=1997-01`, `last_period=2026-08`, `distinct_periods=356` |
| Latest rows | `2026-08` = 3.4, `2026-07` = 3.4, `2026-06` = 3.4, `2026-05` = 3.4, `2026-04` = 3.3 |
| Metadata | Label, `ESTAT`, `2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200`, `{"PL":"Poland"}` |
| Snapshot | `11.8`, `3.1`, `3.4` |
| Series describe | `period string`, `unemployment_rate_pct double` |
| Snapshot describe | Three `double` columns |

## Known drift from the 2026-09-19 scripts

The onboarding scripts are historical records. They were correct on 2026-09-19 and are not edited by this
dossier.

1. **Value count.** `07_eurostat_create.sql` says 355 values through `2026-07`. The live source now has 356
   values through `2026-08`.
2. **Latest month.** Caveat 2 says `2026-08` was not published on 2026-09-19. It is published now. The new
   empty position is `2026-09`.
3. **Snapshot examples.** `07_eurostat_select.sql` examples 2 and 3 use the three-column snapshot view and
   therefore end at `2026-07`. The full series view ends at `2026-08`.
4. **Snapshot name.** `une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table` can be misread as a full wide table. It is a three-column
   spot check.
5. **Licence header.** The create script's header points to
   `https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/about/policies/copyright`, which returns 404. The official page is
   `https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice`.
6. **Catalogue wording.** `open_data/rest_apis/rest-api-sources.md` says the licence is "commonly understood
   to align with CC-BY 4.0, but this has not been independently confirmed". The official notice distinguishes
   editorial content (CC BY 4.0) from statistical data reuse (authorised with attribution under Decision
   2011/833/EU). See [`license-and-attribution.md`](license-and-attribution.md).

## Limits

- **Poland only.** The registration URL fixes `geo=PL`.
- **One sex.** The registration URL fixes `sex=T`.
- **One age class.** The registration URL fixes `age=TOTAL`.
- **One unit.** The registration URL fixes `unit=PC_ACT`.
- **One adjustment.** The registration URL fixes `s_adj=SA`.
- **No status flags in the series view.** The raw `status` struct has two entries for PL, but the decoded view
  does not expose them.
- **No history.** The registration returns the current vintage. Revisions overwrite prior values.
- **Dynamic structs.** `value`, `status`, and `dimension.time.category.index` are structs with one field per
  key. Do not treat them as maps without coercion.
- **Snapshot view is narrow.** It has three columns and ends at `2026-07`.
- **REST table is a registration, not a cache guarantee.** Treat queries as reads against the registered
  endpoint; do not assume a local copy or a vintage.

## Adding another country

There is no runtime parameter on the registered REST table. To add Germany, for example, create a second
registration with `geo=DE` and a distinct table name:

```sql
CREATE LIGHTNING REST TABLE une_rt_m_de FROM EUROSTAT_REST REQUEST(
    endpoint "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&geo=DE&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA&lang=EN",
    method "get",
    response_type "json",
    http_encoding "URLENCODED"
) HEADER (
) BODY ();
```

Then create the same three views with `de` names. This is a live change and is not part of this dossier. For
ad-hoc analysis, the public API is simpler and avoids creating one table per country.

## Security

- The Zetaris API key lives in `.env.local` and is used only by the repository's SQL helpers.
- Never put `ZETARIS_API_KEY` in a browser app, a notebook, a screenshot, or a document.
- The Eurostat endpoint itself needs no key.
- The REST table registration does not add authentication to Eurostat; it adds a Zetaris object that reads
  the public endpoint.

## Teardown

The create script comments out the teardown. If removal is explicitly approved, the views can be dropped with
SQL:

```sql
DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table;
DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table;
DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table;
```

The underlying REST table and Lightning database are removed through the Zetaris Data Explorer; the script
notes that there is no SQL path for those objects. Do not run teardown as part of routine verification.

| Full dataset status flags | 11,291 | 11,291 | PASS |
| Full dataset time categories | 525 | 525 | PASS |
| CORS | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` | Present | PASS |
| Invalid `age=Y15-74` | Empty category and value | Empty | PASS (documented quirk) |
| Invalid `geo=XX` | Empty category and value | Empty | PASS (documented quirk) |

## Coverage of the five-country comparison

Fixed dimensions: `sex=T`, `age=TOTAL`, `unit=PC_ACT`, `s_adj=SA`. Counts are identical for `M` and `F`.

| Country | Values | First | Last | Missing | Missing explanation |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| Poland (`PL`) | 356 | 1997-01 | 2026-08 | 169 | 168 leading months + 2026-09 |
| Germany (`DE`) | 428 | 1991-01 | 2026-08 | 97 | 96 leading months + 2026-09 |
| France (`FR`) | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 | 2026-09 |
| Spain (`ES`) | 485 | 1986-04 | 2026-08 | 40 | 39 leading months + 2026-09 |
| Italy (`IT`) | 524 | 1983-01 | 2026-08 | 1 | 2026-09 |

The full 38-category geography table, with counts and ranges, is in
[`data-dictionary.md`](data-dictionary.md).

## Missing data

### Registered PL slice

The PL slice has 525 time positions and 356 populated values. The 169 missing positions are:

- `1983-01` through `1996-12`: 168 leading months before the Polish series starts.
- `2026-09`: the latest time position, present in the axis but not yet populated.

The source reports these explicitly:

```json
{
  "extension": {
    "positions-with-no-data": {
      "time": [0, 1, 2, "...", 166, 167, 524]
    }
  }
}
```

The array has 169 entries: indices `0`–`167` and `524`.

### Full dataset

The full dataset has 757,828 values across 1,077,300 possible cells. Its
`extension.positions-with-no-data` arrays are empty for every dimension, including `time`. A missing value is
therefore indicated by the absence of a key from `value`, not by an explicit no-data list.

The full dataset's 38 geography categories have very different start dates. For example, Ireland, the
Netherlands, and Sweden have values from `1983-01`; Poland and Romania start in `1997-01`; Bosnia and
Herzegovina starts in `2021-01`; Switzerland's series ends in `2026-06`. These are country-specific coverage
differences, not data corruption.

## Contiguity

For the five-country comparison, the number of populated values equals the number of months between the first
and last populated month:

| Country | Expected months | Observed values | Duplicate periods |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| Poland | 356 | 356 | 0 |
| Germany | 428 | 428 | 0 |
| France | 524 | 524 | 0 |
| Spain | 485 | 485 | 0 |
| Italy | 524 | 524 | 0 |

The PL check is also confirmed in Zetaris:

```text
COUNT(*) = 356
COUNT(DISTINCT period) = 356
MIN(period) = 1997-01
MAX(period) = 2026-08
```

There are no duplicate periods and no interior gaps in the PL series.

## PL/T series profile

| Statistic | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Count | 356 |
| First | `1997-01` = 11.8 |
| Latest | `2026-08` = 3.4 |
| Previous month | `2026-07` = 3.4 |
| Year-over-year | `2025-08` = 3.2; change +0.2 |
| Minimum | `2023-02` = 2.6 |
| Maximum | `2002-08` = 20.5 |
| Mean | 9.47 |
| Median | 9.50 |
| Change since first | -8.4 percentage points |

The series is not monotonic. It rose to a peak of 20.5 in 2002-08, fell through the 2010s, and reached its
minimum of 2.6 in 2023-02 before settling near 3.4 in 2026.

## Status flags

### Full-dataset distribution

| Code | Label | Count |
| :--- | :--- | ---: |
| `b` | break in time series | 1,307 |
| `d` | definition differs (see metadata) | 846 |
| `p` | provisional | 5,832 |
| `u` | low reliability | 3,306 |
| **Total** | | **11,291** |

### Five-country flags

| Country | Flagged months | Details |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| Poland | 2 | `2009-01` = b; `2009-12` = d |
| Germany | 2 | `2005-03` = d; `2009-01` = b |
| France | 3 | `1995-12` = d; `2003-01` = b; `2021-01` = d |
| Spain | 1 | `1995-12` = d |
| Italy | 109 | `1983-01`–`1991-12` = p (108 months); `2004-01` = b |

The flags are stored in the top-level `status` object, keyed by the same flat index as `value`. The
`extension.status.label` object only maps codes to labels. The Zetaris series view does not carry the flags,
so a SQL consumer that needs to exclude provisional or low-reliability values must join back to the raw REST
table.

### Interpretation

- `b` means a break in the time series. Comparisons across the break should be made with care.
- `d` means the definition differs from the standard. Read the ESMS metadata before comparing the value with
  other countries.
- `p` means provisional. The value may be revised.
- `u` means low reliability. The estimate is based on a small sample or otherwise uncertain.

Italy's 108 provisional months from 1983-01 to 1991-12 are the largest block in the five-country comparison.
A consumer that treats all Italian history as equally reliable would overstate confidence in the 1980s and
early 1990s.

## Seasonal adjustment

The registered slice uses `SA`, "Seasonally adjusted data, not calendar adjusted data". The full dataset also
contains:

- `NSA`: unadjusted data, neither seasonally nor calendar adjusted.
- `TC`: trend cycle data.

Do not compare an `SA` series with an `NSA` series without stating the difference. The `SA` series is the
headline monthly indicator, but the `NSA` series is the one that is temporally consistent with the published
quarterly LFS. The ESMS notes that the headline figures in the monthly unemployment news release are
seasonally adjusted.

## Revisions

The source is a current-vintage dataset. Revisions are not optional; they are part of the production process.

### Routine revisions

- New validated data update the already disseminated series.
- Aggregates and components are revised together.
- Monthly series are kept temporally consistent with the quarterly LFS.
- Seasonal adjustment models are reviewed annually, and the annual review can revise seasonally adjusted
  history.
- For routine revisions, data are considered final after six months.

### Major revisions affecting this dossier

| Country | Revision | Published |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Poland | Data revised from January 2019 to June 2023 due to Census 2021 revisions | 2024-03-01 |
| Germany | Data revised back to 2009 due to Census 2021 revisions | 2025-06-03 |
| France | Data revised back to 2003 due to the inclusion of Mayotte | 2026-10-01 |
| Spain | Data revised from January 2021 to December 2023 due to Census 2021 revisions | 2024-05-03 |

The France revision was published on 2026-10-01, less than a month before this verification. It is the most
recent major revision in the five-country set.

### Unscheduled revisions

Eurostat corrects validated errors as soon as the correct data are available. The ESMS records unscheduled
revisions for Lithuania in 2021–2023; those do not affect the five-country comparison but illustrate that the
source can change outside the routine calendar.

## Known source quirks

1. **Invalid codes return empty data, not an HTTP error.** `age=Y15-74` and `geo=XX` both return HTTP 200 with
   an empty category index and an empty `value` object.
2. **The latest time position can be empty.** `2026-09` is in the axis but has no value for the registered
   slice or the five-country comparison.
3. **The snapshot view is three columns.** It is not a wide table and it ends at `2026-07`.
4. **The series view drops status flags.** Use the raw REST table or the API if flags matter.
5. **The full dataset includes non-EU countries.** The United States and Japan are present. Eurostat's general
   reuse permission does not cover commercial reuse of data for countries outside the EU, EFTA, and official
   EU acceding and candidate countries. See [`license-and-attribution.md`](license-and-attribution.md).
6. **The value keys are stringified flat indices.** They are not time labels. For a filtered slice with all
   non-time dimensions at size 1, the key equals the time index; for a multi-dimension slice, it does not.

## Validation commands

### Live source

```bash
curl -sS --compressed \
  'https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA' \
  -o /tmp/eurostat_pl_t.json
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open('/tmp/eurostat_pl_t.json', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    data = json.load(handle)
print('values', len(data['value']))
print('no-data', len(data['extension']['positions-with-no-data']['time']))
print('status', data['status'])
PY
```

Expected:

```text
values 356
no-data 169
status {'312': 'b', '323': 'd'}
```

### Zetaris

```bash
python3 scripts/preflight.py
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(period) AS first_period, MAX(period) AS last_period, COUNT(DISTINCT period) AS distinct_periods FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT period, unemployment_rate_pct FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table ORDER BY period DESC LIMIT 5"
```

Expected:

```text
n=356, first_period=1997-01, last_period=2026-08, distinct_periods=356
2026-08 3.4
2026-07 3.4
2026-06 3.4
2026-05 3.4
2026-04 3.3
```

## Quality verdict

The registered PL slice is complete and internally consistent: 356 values, 356 distinct periods, no duplicate
periods, no interior gaps, and an exact match between the live source and the Zetaris series view. The main
quality caveats are the two status-flagged months, the current-vintage revision model, and the fact that the
Zetaris views do not expose status flags. For the five-country comparison, France and Italy are effectively
complete, Germany and Spain have well-understood start dates, and Poland has the largest leading gap. The
source's overall accuracy is assessed as high by Eurostat, with the caveats described in the ESMS metadata.

# Operations runbook

This runbook covers the Eurostat `une_rt_m` registration and the public API. It does not create, modify, or
delete anything unless a step explicitly says so. Run read-only checks first, and get approval before any
mutation.

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Why |
| :--- | :--- |
| Python 3.9 or later | Runs `scripts/preflight.py`, `scripts/run_sql.py`, and `scripts/onboard.py`. |
| `.env.local` | Holds `ZETARIS_REST_URL`, `ZETARIS_API_KEY`, `ZETARIS_USERNAME`, `ZETARIS_PASSWORD`, and `ZETARIS_USER_AGENT`. |
| Zetaris REST access | The registration and verification queries use the REST channel. |
| `curl` | Fetches the live JSON-stat response. |
| `python3` standard library | Parses JSON without extra packages. |
| Network access to `ec.europa.eu` | Required for live verification and refresh. |

No Node.js runtime is required for the data source or the Zetaris checks. A browser client only needs the
public API.

## Preflight

Run this before any Zetaris work:

```bash
cd /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started
python3 scripts/preflight.py
```

Expected result:

```text
[PASS] env file: /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started/.env.local
[PASS] ZETARIS_API_KEY: [REDACTED] ZETARIS_USERNAME: set
[PASS] ZETARIS_PASSWORD: [REDACTED] ZETARIS_USER_AGENT: set, in the form app_name user@domain.tld
[PASS] REST datasources: HTTP 200
[PASS] REST SELECT 1
[INFO] lightning databases: EUROSTAT_REST, ...
READY
```

If preflight fails, stop and report the missing item. Do not create credentials or change the endpoint to work
around a failure.

## Verify the live source

### Fetch the registered slice

```bash
cd /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started
curl -sS --compressed \
  'https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA' \
  -o /tmp/eurostat_pl_t.json
```

### Check the count, range, missing positions, and status

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json

with open('/tmp/eurostat_pl_t.json', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    data = json.load(handle)

time_index = data['dimension']['time']['category']['index']
index_to_period = {position: period for period, position in time_index.items()}
values = data['value']
keys = sorted(int(key) for key in values)
missing = data['extension']['positions-with-no-data']['time']
status = data['status']

print('updated', data['updated'])
print('values', len(values))
print('first', index_to_period[keys[0]])
print('last', index_to_period[keys[-1]])
print('missing', len(missing))
print('status', status)
PY
```

Expected:

```text
updated 2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200
values 356
first 1997-01
last 2026-08
missing 169
status {'312': 'b', '323': 'd'}
```

If the values differ, record the new count, first/last period, missing count, and status. Update the
verification ledger in [`data-quality.md`](data-quality.md) before drawing conclusions.

### Check the API contract

```bash
curl -sSI \
  'https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA' \
  | sed -n '1,20p'
```

Expected headers include:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET
```

## Verify the Zetaris registration

### Count and range

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(period) AS first_period, MAX(period) AS last_period, COUNT(DISTINCT period) AS distinct_periods FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table"
```

Expected:

```text
['356', '1997-01', '2026-08', '356']
```

### Latest rows

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT period, unemployment_rate_pct FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table ORDER BY period DESC LIMIT 5"
```

Expected:

```text
['2026-08', '3.4']
['2026-07', '3.4']
['2026-06', '3.4']
['2026-05', '3.4']
['2026-04', '3.3']
```

### Metadata

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT dataset_label, dataset_source, last_updated, geo_labels FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table"
```

Expected:

```text
['Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data', 'ESTAT', '2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200', '{"PL":"Poland"}']
```

### Snapshot

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "SELECT rate_1997_01, rate_2025_07, rate_2026_07 FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table"
```

Expected:

```text
['11.8', '3.1', '3.4']
```

### Types

```bash
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "DESCRIBE eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "DESCRIBE eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table"
python3 scripts/run_sql.py -e "DESCRIBE eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table"
```

Expected:

```text
series:   period string, unemployment_rate_pct double
snapshot: rate_1997_01 double, rate_2025_07 double, rate_2026_07 double
metadata: dataset_label string, dataset_source string, last_updated string,
          geo_labels struct<PL:string>, time_index_map struct<...525 fields>
```

## Refresh the registration

The manifest id is `eurostat`. Use `onboard.py` so the dependency order and the create script are resolved from
the manifest rather than typed by hand.

### Show the plan

```bash
cd /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started
python3 scripts/onboard.py plan eurostat
```

### Dry run

```bash
python3 scripts/onboard.py run eurostat --dry-run
```

Review the statement list. The create script includes:

- `CREATE LIGHTNING DATABASE EUROSTAT_REST`
- `CREATE SCHEMASTORE CONTAINER eurostat`
- `CREATE LIGHTNING REST TABLE une_rt_m_pl`
- Three `CREATE SCHEMASTORE VIEW` statements

### Re-run with skip-exists

After approval, and only if the objects already exist or the intent is to refresh the registration:

```bash
python3 scripts/onboard.py run eurostat --skip-exists
```

`--skip-exists` skips duplicate-object errors. Without it, the run stops at the first object that already
exists. A refresh does not rewrite the view definitions if they already exist; to change a view, drop and
recreate it deliberately.

### Verify after refresh

Re-run the count, range, metadata, snapshot, and type checks above. Compare the live source count with the
Zetaris count. They must match.

## Teardown

Teardown is destructive. Get explicit approval before running it.

### Show the teardown plan

```bash
python3 scripts/onboard.py teardown eurostat
```

### Execute

```bash
python3 scripts/onboard.py teardown eurostat --yes
```

The runner drops the views it can derive from the create script. It leaves REST/file registrations, Lightning
databases, and SchemaStore containers for manual cleanup and lists them in its output. The create script's own
teardown section comments out only the three `DROP VIEW` statements. The REST table and `EUROSTAT_REST`
database are removed through the Zetaris Data Explorer.

Do not use `--drop-namespace` for this source; it is a USL option and there is no USL namespace here.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Preflight 401 | Bad `ZETARIS_API_KEY` | Re-check `.env.local`; do not print the key. |
| Preflight 400 | Bad `X-Org-ID` or non-UUID `X-Request-ID` | Check the REST helper configuration. |
| `Operation not permitted` before HTTP | Local network restriction | Request elevated execution for the read-only preflight; do not change the endpoint. |
| Empty API result | Invalid dimension code | Check `age`, `sex`, `geo`, `unit`, and `s_adj` against the valid codes. |
| `dimension.age.category.index = {}` | Invalid age, such as `Y15-74` | Use `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, or `Y25-74`. |
| `value = {}` | Invalid code or no data for the slice | Re-check the URL; the API returns HTTP 200 even for empty results. |
| CORS error in a browser | Eurostat changed CORS or the request is malformed | Check the response headers; a proxy/BFF would be a separate approved change. |
| Series view empty | View creation failed or the raw table is empty | Check `DESCRIBE` and `SELECT * FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl LIMIT 1`. |
| `DATATYPE_MISMATCH` on `explode()` | Dynamic-key object was not coerced | Apply `from_json(to_json(...), 'map<...>')` to both `value` and `dimension.time.category.index`. |
| Latest row is `2026-07` | Querying the snapshot view | Use `une_rt_m_pl_series_table`; the snapshot view ends at `2026-07`. |
| Latest row is `2026-08`, but `2026-09` is expected | Normal reporting lag | Check the source `updated` timestamp and the next release. |
| Count mismatch | Source revised or registration stale | Re-run the live count and the Zetaris count; refresh if needed. |

## Security

- Keep `ZETARIS_API_KEY` in `.env.local`. Never print it, paste it into a document, or put it in a browser app.
- The Eurostat API needs no key. Do not add one.
- Do not commit `.env.local`, downloaded responses, or query outputs that contain credentials.
- Use the least-privileged Zetaris account that can read the objects. Creating, dropping, and granting are
  administrative actions.
- Do not run teardown or refresh commands without explicit approval.

## Change log

| Date | Change | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2026-10-23 | Initial verification of the live source, Zetaris series view, metadata view, and snapshot view. | 356 values, 356 rows, metadata timestamp, snapshot values. |
| 2026-10-23 | Documented the 2026-09-19 script drift. | Live source has 356 values through 2026-08; script says 355 through 2026-07. |
| 2026-10-23 | Corrected the licence reference to the official copyright notice. | Old `/about/policies/copyright` URL returns 404. |

# License and attribution

This document records the official Eurostat reuse terms and the attribution this dossier uses. It is a
summary for engineering use, not legal advice. The authoritative source is the Eurostat copyright notice:

- <https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice>

## Two different regimes

Eurostat distinguishes **editorial content** from **statistical data**:

| Material | Terms |
| :--- | :--- |
| Editorial content (text, photographs, graphics, etc.) | Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Reuse is allowed with source acknowledgement and an indication of any changes. |
| Statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools | Reuse for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged. The reuse policy is implemented by the European Commission's Decision of 12 December 2011 (2011/833/EU). |

The dataset in this dossier is statistical data. Do not describe it as "CC BY 4.0 data". The correct statement is
that reuse is authorised with attribution under Decision 2011/833/EU, subject to the exceptions below.

## Exceptions

The general permission does not cover:

- **Third-party material.** Material whose copyright is identified as belonging to a third party, such as
  photos or illustrations from other rights holders. Permission must be obtained from the rights holder.
- **Logos and trademarks.** These are excluded unless they are redistributed as an integral part of an
  unchanged Eurostat publication.
- **Translations and modifications.** If you translate or modify the data or text, you must state this clearly
  to the end user and include a disclaimer that Eurostat is not responsible for the result.
- **Data for countries outside the EU, EFTA, and official EU acceding and candidate countries.** Commercial
  reuse is not allowed. Examples include data for the United States, Japan, and China. Non-commercial reuse is
  allowed. A commercial user must remove those countries from the table before reuse.
- **Trade data from Liechtenstein and Switzerland** as declaring countries from 1995 onwards, for HS, SITC,
  BEC, NSTR, and national commodity classifications. Commercial reuse of those declared flows is not allowed.
- **Trade data from Austria** as a declaring country at the 8-digit Combined Nomenclature level. Commercial
  reuse of those declared flows is not allowed.

The last two exceptions concern trade data and do not apply to `une_rt_m`. The country exception does apply to
the **full** `une_rt_m` dataset, because it includes the United States, Japan, and other non-EU/EFTA countries.
The registered PL slice and the five-country comparison (PL, DE, FR, ES, IT) are inside the permitted set.

## Commercial reuse

There is no special procedure and no written licence required. Download the material and use it, unless the
material falls under an exception above. For a commercial product that uses the full dataset, remove the
non-EU/EFTA/candidate countries first, or use a filtered request that only returns permitted countries.

## How to cite

### Dataset DOI

The canonical form is:

```text
Source: [DOI], [access date]
```

For this dataset:

```text
Source: 10.2908/UNE_RT_M, 2026-10-23.
```

The DOI URL is:

- <https://doi.org/10.2908/UNE_RT_M>

### Customised dataset

If you filter or otherwise customise the dataset, cite the datacode link instead of the DOI:

```text
Source: [Eurostat dataset datacode link], [access date]
```

For example:

```text
Source: Eurostat, une_rt_m (unemployment rate, monthly),
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/une_rt_m/default/table, accessed 2026-10-23.
```

### Other products

For interactive tools, visualisations, webpages, Statistics Explained articles, and PDFs, the form is:

```text
Source: Eurostat, [Title of the product], [link to the product], [access date].
```

## Attribution used in this dossier

The dossier uses the DOI form in its headers and the customised form where a filtered series is described:

```text
Source: 10.2908/UNE_RT_M, 2026-10-23.
```

```text
Source: Eurostat, une_rt_m (unemployment rate, monthly),
https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/une_rt_m/default/table, accessed 2026-10-23.
```

If a downstream artifact modifies the data, add a clear statement such as:

```text
Based on Eurostat data. The modifications are the responsibility of the author.
Eurostat is not responsible for the modified data or for any interpretation of it.
```

Do not imply that Eurostat endorses the modification, the application, or the analysis.

## No affiliation

This repository is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Eurostat or the European Commission.
Eurostat is the source of the data; the repository is an independent engineering example.

## Catalogue correction

`open_data/rest_apis/rest-api-sources.md` currently says the licence is "commonly understood to align with
CC-BY 4.0, but this has not been independently confirmed". That wording conflates editorial content with
statistical data. Replace the section 7 licence line with:

```text
- **Licence:** Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools is authorised
  for commercial and non-commercial purposes provided the source is acknowledged, under the European
  Commission reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU). Editorial content is CC BY 4.0. Commercial reuse of data for
  countries outside the EU, EFTA, and official EU acceding and candidate countries is not allowed. See the
  [Eurostat license and attribution dossier](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/license-and-attribution.md).
```

Add a full-dossier pointer:

```text
- **Full dossier:** [`docs/data-sources/eurostat/README.md`](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/README.md)
```

Keep the source's `Verified` status and the script path unchanged. The correction is about the licence
description, not about whether the registration ran.

## Dataset-specific notes

- `une_rt_m` is a Eurostat-produced statistical dataset. The dataset page identifies Eurostat as the source.
- The registered slice contains only Poland. The full dataset contains the United States, Japan, and other
  non-EU/EFTA countries, so the commercial country exception matters for full-dataset reuse.
- The dataset may contain estimates and provisional values. Attribution does not imply accuracy; see
  [`data-quality.md`](data-quality.md) for status flags and revisions.
- The source's metadata and structure change over time. Cite the access date so a later reader can tell which
  vintage was used.
- The old create-script header points to `https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/about/policies/copyright`, which
  returns 404. Use the official notice URL above.

182: 4. For each time position, compute the flat index with the other dimensions fixed at index `0`:

184:    ```text
185:    flat = time_position * stride[time_dimension]
186:    ```

188:    This is valid for a request that filters every non-time dimension to one category. The registered slice
189:    does exactly that.
190: 5. Read `value[String(flat)]`.
191: 6. Keep only finite numeric values.
192: 7. Sort ascending by period label.

238:   const observations: Observation[] = [];
239: 
240:   for (const [period, position] of Object.entries(timeIndex)) {
241:     const flat = position * strides[timeDimension];
242:     const value = dataset.value[String(flat)];
243:     if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) {
244:       observations.push({ period, rate: value });
245:     }
246:   }
247: 
248:   return observations.sort((left, right) => left.period.localeCompare(right.period));
249: }

165: ### Revision policy
166: 
167: Eurostat's monthly unemployment revision policy has three layers:
168: 
169: 1. **Routine revisions.** New validated data update the already disseminated series. Aggregates and components

191: ## Methodology
192: 
193: ### Data source
194: 
195: The EU-LFS is the main data source. Where a country compiles only quarterly LFS data, Eurostat complements it
196: with a monthly indicator from the national public employment authority. The monthly series is then produced
197: through a harmonised process.
198: 
199: For Poland, the ESMS states that quarterly LFS data are combined with monthly registered unemployment data
200: using a **Denton temporal disaggregation** model. For the most recent months, where LFS data are not yet
201: available, the monthly benchmark factors are forecast using **seasonal ARIMA regression** models. The
202: provisional estimates are the product of those factors and the available registered unemployment figures.
203: This is why the Polish series can be revised when new LFS data arrive.
204: 
205: ### Seasonal adjustment
206: 
207: For countries that deliver monthly unemployment inputs, Eurostat performs the seasonal adjustment at a
208: disaggregated level (country by sex by age group, indirect approach) using **TRAMO/SEATS**. Germany uses
209: **X-13** for trend calculation. The registered Zetaris slice uses the `SA` series, not `NSA` or `TC`.
210: 
211: ### Timeliness
212: 
213: Monthly seasonally adjusted unemployment rates are published approximately **31 days after the end of the
214: reference month**. The source timestamp is the authoritative record of when the current vintage was produced.

213: ## Missing and status semantics
214: 
215: ### Missing values
216: 
217: There are two different signals:
218: 
219: 1. **`extension.positions-with-no-data`** is an explicit list of positions that the source declares as having
220:    no data. For the PL slice, `time` has 169 positions: `0` through `167` and `524`. The other dimensions have
221:    empty arrays.
222: 2. **Absence from `value`** is the general signal. The full dataset has no global `positions-with-no-data.time`
223:    list, so a missing flat index is simply not present in `value`.
224: 
225: Do not infer missingness from a zero or an empty string. The source uses absent keys, not sentinel values.
226: 
227: ### Status codes
228: 
229: | Code | Label | Full-dataset count | Meaning |
230: | :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
231: | `b` | break in time series | 1,307 | The series has a break at this observation. |
232: | `d` | definition differs (see metadata) | 846 | The definition differs from the standard; consult metadata. |
233: | `p` | provisional | 5,832 | The value is provisional and may be revised. |
234: | `u` | low reliability | 3,306 | The value has low reliability. |
235: 
236: The top-level `status` object is keyed by the same flat index as `value`. The `extension.status.label` object
237: maps the codes to their labels; it does not carry per-observation flags.
238: 
239: ### Status flags in the five-country comparison
240: 
241: | Country | Flagged months | Codes |
242: | :--- | ---: | :--- |
243: | Poland | 2 | `2009-01` = b; `2009-12` = d |
244: | Germany | 2 | `2005-03` = d; `2009-01` = b |
245: | France | 3 | `1995-12` = d; `2003-01` = b; `2021-01` = d |
246: | Spain | 1 | `1995-12` = d |
247: | Italy | 109 | `1983-01`–`1991-12` = p (108 months); `2004-01` = b |
248: 
249: The flags are attached to the observations. The Zetaris series view drops them, so a SQL consumer that needs
250: to exclude provisional or low-reliability values must join back to the raw REST table.
251: 
252: ## Decode technique
253: 
254: ### Flat index
255: 
256: JSON-stat stores observations in a flat array (or, here, a sparse object keyed by the flat index). The flat
257: index is:
258: 
259: ```text
260: flat = sum(index[d] * stride[d])
261: stride[d] = product(size[d + 1 :])
262: ```
263: 
264: For the registered PL slice, every dimension except `time` has size 1, so the flat index equals the time
265: index. `2026-08` has time index `523`, so its flat index is `523`.
266: 
267: For the full dataset, the stride vector is:
268: 
269: ```text
270: [1077300, 359100, 119700, 59850, 19950, 525, 1]
271: ```
272: 
273: For the full-dataset cell `freq=M`, `s_adj=SA`, `age=TOTAL`, `unit=PC_ACT`, `sex=T`, `geo=PL`,
274: `time=2026-08`, the indices are `0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 22, 523`, and the flat index is:
275: 
276: ```text
277: 1*359100 + 1*59850 + 22*525 + 523 = 431023
278: ```
279: 
280: ### SQL decode
281: 
282: The registered series view uses two coercions and an equality join:
283: 
284: ```sql
285: SELECT
286:     time_label AS period,
287:     CAST(rate_value AS DOUBLE) AS unemployment_rate_pct
288: FROM eurostat_rest.une_rt_m_pl
289: LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(value), 'map<string,double>')) AS time_key, rate_value
290: LATERAL VIEW explode(from_json(to_json(dimension.time.category.index), 'map<string,bigint>')) AS time_label, time_index_value
291: WHERE CAST(time_key AS INT) = time_index_value;
292: ```
293: 
294: Both `value` and `dimension.time.category.index` must be coerced. A plain `explode()` on either field fails
295: with a `DATATYPE_MISMATCH` because both are inferred as structs, not maps. The join compares the stringified
296: flat index in `value` with the integer time index.
297: 
298: ### Python decode
299: 
300: A minimal, dependency-free decoder for the registered slice:
301: 
302: ```python
303: import json
304: from urllib.request import urlopen
305: 
306: URL = (
307:     "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m"
308:     "?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA"
309: )
310: 
311: with urlopen(URL, timeout=60) as response:
312:     dataset = json.load(response)
313: 
314: time_index = dataset["dimension"]["time"]["category"]["index"]
315: index_to_period = {position: period for period, position in time_index.items()}
316: rows = sorted(
317:     (index_to_period[int(key)], value)
318:     for key, value in dataset["value"].items()
319: )
320: for period, value in rows[-3:]:
321:     print(period, value)
322: ```
323: 
324: The decoder assumes the filtered slice has size 1 on every non-time dimension. For a multi-dimension slice,
325: compute the flat index with the stride formula instead of treating the `value` key as a time index.
326:

- **REST:** the key is `ZETARIS_API_KEY` in `.env.local`, created by the user in the Zetaris GUI. Never create, request, print, log or put it in a URL.
- **OpenAPI spec:** fetch it fresh from `/redoc/docs.yaml` using Basic auth (`ZETARIS_USERNAME` and `ZETARIS_PASSWORD` from `.env.local`), not the bearer key. See section 6.4 of the connection guide.
- **Finding `.env.local`:** it is the only env file; do not use `.env`. It is gitignored, so a git worktree has none. Every script in `scripts/` (Python and Deno) already looks in the repo root and then the top-level checkout. For your own shell commands, use the snippet in the preflight section.

## Preflight check

Run this before any Zetaris work in a new session, and report what is missing. Do not install anything, create credentials, or start work until the user has seen the result. Ask before installing.

Run `python3 scripts/preflight.py` (add `--jdbc --jar <path>` for JDBC). It is read-only and covers the checklist below; the list is what it checks and why. Run SQL files with `python3 scripts/run_sql.py FILE` (`--dry-run` first, `--skip-exists` to re-run, `--channel jdbc` for JDBC); see `scripts/HOWTO.md`.

1. **Credentials.** Find `.env.local` (see "Connect first"). Check that these names are set, without printing values: `ZETARIS_API_KEY` for REST, and `ZETARIS_USERNAME` / `ZETARIS_PASSWORD` for the OpenAPI spec and for JDBC. Also note `ZETARIS_JDBC_JAR` (driver path, JDBC only) and `ZETARIS_USER_AGENT` (needed by any create script containing the `YOUR_APP_NAME YOUR_CONTACT_EMAIL` placeholder).
   ```bash
   ENV="$(dirname "$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" && pwd)")/.env.local"
   set -a; . "$ENV"; set +a
   for v in ZETARIS_API_KEY ZETARIS_USERNAME ZETARIS_PASSWORD; do [ -n "$(printenv "$v")" ] && echo "$v set" || echo "$v MISSING"; done
   ```
2. **REST.** `GET /datasource/datasources` returns 200, and `SELECT 1` through `/sql-editor/sqls/run` returns `1`. A 401 means a bad key; a 400 means a bad `X-Org-ID` or a non-UUID `X-Request-ID`. If localhost fails with `Operation not permitted` before an HTTP response, treat it as a possible command-environment network restriction, not an API or credential failure. Request approved/elevated execution for the same read-only preflight and retry when available. If access is unavailable or denied, report the blocker and stop; do not change the endpoint or credentials to work around it.
3. **JDBC** (only if the user wants JDBC):
   - **Endpoint:** `nc -z localhost 10000` succeeds.
   - **Java:** JDK 11 or later. On macOS `java` can be a stub that reports "Unable to locate a Java Runtime" even when a Homebrew JDK exists. Check `/usr/libexec/java_home`, then `/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home`, and export `JAVA_HOME`. If none exists, offer `brew install openjdk@17`. The `temurin` cask needs `sudo`, which the agent cannot enter.
   - **Python:** a venv (`.venv` is gitignored) with `jaydebeapi` importable.
   - **Driver JAR:** ask the user for the full path and confirm the file exists. Never assume a location.
   - **Query:** connect with `jdbc:zetaris:lightning@localhost:10000` and class `com.zetaris.lightning.jdbc.LightningDriver`, then run `SELECT 1`.
4. **Instance state.** `SHOW DATASOURCES` does not list Lightning-registered sources (REST, file). Also run `SHOW LIGHTNING DATABASES`. For USL, run `SHOW NAMESPACES OR TABLES IN lightning.metastore`; an empty result is normal on a clean instance, but a failing `CREATE NAMESPACE` on a missing parent means `lightning.metastore` is not initialized (see the USL note under "Writing SQL").
5. **Report** a short pass/fail list, and stop on any failure.

## Writing SQL

- Zetaris Lightning SQL only. Not Spark SQL or Hive SQL, and never start a local Spark session.
- One statement per call, no trailing semicolon, qualified names (`<source>.<table>`). A `_create.sql` script holds many statements; `scripts/run_sql.py` splits and sends them for you.
- **USL:** `lightning.metastore` must exist before `CREATE NAMESPACE IF NOT EXISTS lightning.metastore.<name>` works; check with `SHOW NAMESPACES OR TABLES IN lightning.metastore` (on an uninitialized instance the statement fails with "parent namespace : metastore is not existing"). A multi-table `COMPILE USL` must be sent as one whole statement, so do not split it on `;`. It works over JDBC and REST that way. Use `SHOW DQ ALL INVALID TABLE <namespace.usl.table>` (the `TABLE` clause is required).
- Read `docs/guides/zetaris-lightning-sql-commands.md` for syntax and `docs/guides/zetaris-lightning-sql-companion.md` for confirmed gotchas and platform limitations before writing new SQL.

## Running scripts

Use `scripts/onboard.py` to onboard sources and USL models with their dependencies, and `scripts/run_sql.py` to run any single `_create.sql` / `_select.sql` file or ad hoc SQL. Do not hand-roll a splitter. See `scripts/HOWTO.md` for options.

- **Dry-run first** (`--dry-run`) and show the user the statement list. Create scripts change the instance, so get a clear go-ahead before running one for real.
- **User-agent.** `ZETARIS_USER_AGENT` must be `app_name user@domain.tld`: an app name and a contact e-mail. `company_dns` V4 gives anything vaguer (a bare name, a library default, none) a very strict rate limit, and SEC EDGAR needs a real contact. Never send the `YOUR_APP_NAME YOUR_CONTACT_EMAIL` placeholder, and do not invent or reuse a contact email. If `ZETARIS_USER_AGENT` is not set, or is not in that form, ask the user which value to send, then pass it for the run or have them add it to `.env.local`. The runner refuses the placeholder and any value without a contact e-mail.
- **Re-runs.** `--skip-exists` skips "already exists" errors, so a script can be run again on an instance that already has some of its objects. Without it the run stops at the first duplicate.
- **JDBC.** `--channel jdbc` needs the driver JAR from `--jar` or `ZETARIS_JDBC_JAR`. Ask the user for the path; never assume one. The runner finds a Homebrew JDK and hops into `.venv` itself.
- **Order and dependencies.** The approach is: onboard the data sources first, then create and activate a USL over them. Every source and USL model, with the sources it `requires`, is declared once in `open_data/manifest.json`. Use `python3 scripts/onboard.py --list` to see them, `plan <id>...` to see the resolved order, and `run <id>... --dry-run` then `run <id>...` to onboard them with their dependencies first. Never work out the order by hand or from HOWTO prose. A `known_to_fail` source needs `--allow-known-to-fail`. When you add a create script, add it to the manifest (`onboard.py --check` validates it).
- **Teardown and restarts.** When the user asks to clean up or start over, confirm the scope first (instance objects, local setup such as `.venv`, any published viewer), then use `python3 scripts/onboard.py teardown <id>...`. Do not hand-write DROP statements. Show the plan (it also pulls in sources that `require` the target), wait for a go-ahead, then re-run with `--yes`. Do not pipe a script that changes the instance through a filter such as `grep` on its first run; a filter error hides the output while the statements still run. After it finishes, report what only the Zetaris Data Explorer can remove (REST and file tables, Lightning databases, containers) and say that a re-run needs `--skip-exists` if they are left. `--drop-namespace` also removes every USL in the namespace, so only use it when asked.
- **Verify after creating**, as in `open_data/rest_apis/HOWTO.md` section 2: compare Zetaris row counts with an independent check against the source API.

## Safety

- Start read-only (`SHOW`, `DESCRIBE`, `SELECT`). Ask before anything that creates, drops, grants or writes.
- Keep passwords and keys out of prompts, logs, source files and commits.
- Do not call port 8889 on a local instance.
- Least privilege: an agent that only reads should run as a non-administrator user, with creating, updating and deleting left to administrators. If a statement is refused for lack of privilege, report it and ask for the right access; do not switch to an administrator login unless the user tells you to. See `docs/guides/permissions.md`.
- Sources under `known_to_fail/` are documented failures, and `rate_limited/` sources should be run deliberately, not repeatedly.

## Adding or changing sources

Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`: the `_create.sql` / `_select.sql` pattern, the `known_to_fail/` write-up format, and license verification. Source HOWTOs live in `open_data/*/HOWTO.md`.
