1: # Eurostat Statistics API reference
2: 
3: ## Endpoint
4: 
5: | Property | Value |
6: | :--- | :--- |
7: | Base URL | `https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/` |
8: | Dataset path | `une_rt_m` |
9: | Method | `GET` |
10: | Authentication | None |
11: | Registration | None |
12: | Response format | JSON-stat 2.0 when `format=JSON` |
13: | CORS | Enabled (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) |
14: | Typical content type | `application/json` |
15: 
16: The canonical request for the registered Zetaris slice is:
17: 
18: ```text
19: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA
20: ```
21: 
22: ## Parameters
23: 
24: | Parameter | Required | Values used here | Meaning |
25: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
26: | `format` | Recommended | `JSON` | Return JSON-stat instead of SDMX or another format. |
27: | `lang` | Recommended | `EN` | Language for labels and metadata. |
28: | `freq` | Optional | `M` | Monthly frequency. The dataset contains only `M`. |
29: | `s_adj` | Optional | `SA` | Seasonal adjustment. Full codes: `NSA`, `SA`, `TC`. |
30: | `age` | Optional | `TOTAL` | Age class. Full codes: `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, `Y25-74`. |
31: | `unit` | Optional | `PC_ACT` | Unit. Full codes: `THS_PER`, `PC_ACT`. |
32: | `sex` | Optional | `T` | Sex. Full codes: `T`, `M`, `F`. |
33: | `geo` | Optional | `PL` | Geography. Full dataset has 38 categories. |
34: | `time` | Optional | Omitted | Time filter. The registration returns the full 525-month axis. |
35: 
36: Omitting a dimension returns all of its categories. The API does not require every dimension to be filtered.
37: The registered Zetaris slice fixes six dimensions and leaves `time` unfiltered.
38: 
39: ### Fixed dimensions in the registration
40: 
41: | Dimension | Value | Why |
42: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
43: | `freq` | `M` | The dataset is monthly. |
44: | `s_adj` | `SA` | The registration uses the headline seasonally adjusted series. |
45: | `age` | `TOTAL` | The registration uses the total age class. |
46: | `unit` | `PC_ACT` | The registration uses rates, not levels. |
47: | `sex` | `T` | The registration uses the total sex. |
48: | `geo` | `PL` | The registration is a Poland example. |
49: 
50: ## Exact request URLs
51: 
52: ### Registered slice
53: 
54: ```text
55: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA
56: ```
57: 
58: ### Browser template
59: 
60: ```text
61: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=M&s_adj=SA&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&sex={sex}&geo={geo}
62: ```
63: 
64: Replace `{sex}` with `T`, `M`, or `F`, and `{geo}` with a supported country code such as `PL`, `DE`, `FR`,
65: `ES`, or `IT`.
66: 
67: ### Full dataset
68: 
69: ```text
70: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m?format=JSON&lang=EN
71: ```
72: 
73: The full response is about 10 MB uncompressed at the time of verification. It is useful for exploration but
74: too large for a browser page that only needs one series.
75: 
76: ## Response shape
77: 
78: A filtered response has 11 top-level fields:
79: 
80: ```text
81: version, class, label, source, updated, value, status, id, size, dimension, extension
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Top-level fields
85: 
86: | Field | Type | Notes |
87: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
88: | `version` | string | `2.0`. |
89: | `class` | string | `dataset`. |
90: | `label` | string | Dataset title. |
91: | `source` | string | `ESTAT`. |
92: | `updated` | string | Source timestamp. |
93: | `value` | object | Sparse observations keyed by stringified flat index. |
94: | `status` | object | Optional status flags keyed by the same flat index. |
95: | `id` | array | Dimension order. |
96: | `size` | array | Dimension cardinalities. |
97: | `dimension` | object | Category indexes and labels per dimension. |
98: | `extension` | object | Annotations, no-data positions, and status labels. |
99: 
100: ### Filtered slice dimensions
101: 
102: For the PL/T request, `id` and `size` are:
103: 
104: ```text
105: id:   ["freq", "s_adj", "age", "unit", "sex", "geo", "time"]
106: size: [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 525]
107: ```
108: 
109: The time axis has 525 categories, but only 356 have values. `value` is sparse; it does not contain keys for
110: the 169 empty positions.
111: 
112: ### Response excerpt
113: 
114: ```text
115: {
116:   "version": "2.0",
117:   "class": "dataset",
118:   "label": "Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data",
119:   "source": "ESTAT",
120:   "updated": "2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200",
121:   "value": {
122:     "168": 11.8,
123:     "169": 11.5,
124:     ...
125:     "523": 3.4
126:   },
127:   "status": {
128:     "312": "b",
129:     "323": "d"
130:   },
131:   "id": ["freq", "s_adj", "age", "unit", "sex", "geo", "time"],
132:   "size": [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 525],
133:   "dimension": {
134:     "time": {
135:       "label": "Time",
136:       "category": {
137:         "index": {
138:           "1983-01": 0,
139:           ...
140:           "1997-01": 168,
141:           ...
142:           "2026-08": 523,
143:           "2026-09": 524
144:         },
145:         "label": {
146:           "1983-01": "1983-01",
147:           ...
148:         }
149:       }
150:     },
151:     ...
152:   },
153:   "extension": {
154:     "datastructure": {
155:       "id": "UNE_RT_M",
156:       "agencyId": "ESTAT",
157:       "version": "156.0"
158:     },
159:     "positions-with-no-data": {
160:       "time": [0, 1, ..., 167, 524]
161:     },
162:     "status": {
163:       "label": {
164:         "b": "break in time series",
165:         "d": "definition differs (see metadata)"
166:       }
167:     }
168:   }
169: }
170: ```
171: 
172: The excerpt is illustrative; the real `value` object has 356 entries and the real `dimension.time.category.index`
173: has 525 entries.
174: 
175: ## JSON-stat decoding
176: 
177: ### Algorithm
178: 
179: 1. Read `id` and `size`.
180: 2. Build `stride[d] = product(size[d + 1:])`.
181: 3. Invert `dimension.time.category.index` so the integer position maps to a period label.
182: 4. For each time position, compute the flat index with the other dimensions fixed at index `0`:
183: 
184:    ```text
185:    flat = time_position * stride[time_dimension]
186:    ```
187: 
188:    This is valid for a request that filters every non-time dimension to one category. The registered slice
189:    does exactly that.
190: 5. Read `value[String(flat)]`.
191: 6. Keep only finite numeric values.
192: 7. Sort ascending by period label.
193: 
194: For the registered slice, every non-time dimension has size 1, so the flat index equals the time position.
195: `2026-08` has position `523`, so its value is `value["523"]`.
196: 
197: ### TypeScript decoder for a filtered request
198: 
199: ```ts
200: export interface JsonStatDataset {
201:   version: string;
202:   class: "dataset";
203:   label: string;
204:   source: string;
205:   updated: string;
206:   value: Record<string, number>;
207:   status?: Record<string, string>;
208:   id: string[];
209:   size: number[];
210:   dimension: Record<string, {
211:     label: string;
212:     category: {
213:       index: Record<string, number>;
214:       label: Record<string, string>;
215:     };
216:   }>;
217:   extension?: {
218:     status?: { label?: Record<string, string> };
219:     "positions-with-no-data"?: { time?: number[] };
220:   };
221: }
222: 
223: export interface Observation {
224:   period: string;
225:   rate: number;
226: }
227: 
228: export function decodeSeries(dataset: JsonStatDataset): Observation[] {
229:   const timeDimension = dataset.id.indexOf("time");
230:   if (timeDimension === -1) {
231:     throw new Error("JSON-stat response has no time dimension");
232:   }
233: 
234:   const strides = dataset.size.map((_, index) =>
235:     dataset.size.slice(index + 1).reduce((product, size) => product * size, 1),
236:   );
237:   const timeIndex = dataset.dimension.time.category.index;
238:   const observations: Observation[] = [];
239: 
240:   for (const [period, position] of Object.entries(timeIndex)) {
241:     const flat = position * strides[timeDimension];
242:     const value = dataset.value[String(flat)];
243:     if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) {
244:       observations.push({ period, rate: value });
245:     }
246:   }
247: 
248:   return observations.sort((left, right) => left.period.localeCompare(right.period));
249: }
250: ```
251: 
252: ### Python decoder for a filtered request
253: 
254: ```python
255: import json
256: from urllib.request import urlopen
257: 
258: URL = (
259:     "https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m"
260:     "?format=JSON&lang=EN&geo=PL&sex=T&age=TOTAL&unit=PC_ACT&s_adj=SA"
261: )
262: 
263: with urlopen(URL, timeout=60) as response:
264:     dataset = json.load(response)
265: 
266: time_index = dataset["dimension"]["time"]["category"]["index"]
267: index_to_period = {position: period for period, position in time_index.items()}
268: rows = sorted(
269:     (index_to_period[int(key)], value)
270:     for key, value in dataset["value"].items()
271: )
272: print(rows[0], rows[-1])
273: ```
274: 
275: ### General flat-index decoder
276: 
277: For a response with more than one non-time category, compute the flat index with the full formula:
278: 
279: ```text
280: flat = sum(category_index[d] * stride[d] for d in dimensions)
281: ```
282: 
283: Do not assume that the `value` key is a time index unless every other dimension has size 1.
284: 
285: ## Invalid codes
286: 
287: Eurostat does **not** return an HTTP error for an invalid dimension code. It returns HTTP 200 with an empty
288: category and an empty value object. Verified examples:
289: 
290: | Request | Observed |
291: | :--- | :--- |
292: | `age=Y15-74` | `dimension.age.category.index = {}`; `value = {}` |
293: | `geo=XX` | `dimension.geo.category.index = {}`; `value = {}` |
294: 
295: This looks like "no data available" rather than "wrong parameter". Validate codes against the allowlists before
296: requesting. The valid age codes are `TOTAL`, `Y_LT25`, and `Y25-74`; `Y15-74` is not valid for this dataset.
297: 
298: ## Errors, CORS, and limits
299: 
300: ### HTTP and network errors
301: 
302: - A malformed URL or unsupported format can return a 4xx response.
303: - A server-side problem can return a 5xx response.
304: - A network failure or a CORS change appears as a browser fetch rejection, not as a JSON error.
305: - The API does not use an API key, so there is no 401 path for this source.
306: 
307: ### CORS
308: 
309: The live response includes:
310: 
311: ```text
312: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
313: Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET
314: Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Accept, X-Requested-With
315: ```
316: 
317: This permits direct browser requests. If Eurostat changes the CORS policy, a browser client needs a proxy or
318: a server-side component. The repository's registered Zetaris table is not a browser proxy.
319: 
320: ### Rate limits and caching
321: 
322: The source is public and does not publish a numeric rate limit in the response. Treat it as a shared public
323: service:
324: 
325: - Request one series at a time.
326: - Cache responses for a short period, such as five minutes.
327: - Do not loop over all 38 countries and 3 sex codes on every page load.
328: - Do not fetch the full 10 MB dataset for a single-series view.
329: 
330: The full dataset is 757,828 values and is not appropriate for a browser page that needs one country/sex pair.
331: 
332: ## Data freshness and revisions
333: 
334: - `updated` is the authoritative source timestamp for the current vintage.
335: - The latest PL month is `2026-08`; `2026-09` is present but empty.
336: - Eurostat publishes monthly data approximately 31 days after the reference month.
337: - Routine revisions, annual seasonal-adjustment reviews, and major revisions can change historical values.
338: - The API does not expose a vintage history. Store the `updated` value alongside any derived artifact if
339:   reproducibility matters.
340: 
341: ## References
342: 
343: - [Eurostat API Statistics guide](https://wikis.ec.europa.eu/display/EUROSTATHELP/API+Statistics+-+data+query)
344: - [JSON-stat specification](https://json-stat.org/)
345: - [Eurostat ESMS metadata for `une_rt_m`](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/en/une_rt_m_esms.htm)
346: - [Eurostat copyright notice](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice)
347: - [Dataset DOI](https://doi.org/10.2908/UNE_RT_M)

1: # Eurostat CRUD
2: 
3: A small Angular 22 example that saves Eurostat unemployment-rate filters in the browser and
4: fetches the matching observations from the public Eurostat API. It is a standalone, zoneless
5: application with no backend, authentication, database, or Zetaris API key.
6: 
7: The verified dataset notes live in the repository dossier:
8: [`docs/data-sources/eurostat/`](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/README.md).
9: 
10: ## Run locally
11: 
12: Requires Node.js 26 and npm 11.
13: 
14: ```bash
15: npm install
16: npm start
17: ```
18: 
19: Open `http://localhost:4200/`. The development server reloads on source changes.
20: 
21: ```bash
22: npm test -- --watch=false   # Vitest unit tests
23: npm run build               # production bundle in dist/
24: ```
25: 
26: ## Routes
27: 
28: | Route | Purpose |
29: | --- | --- |
30: | `/series` | List saved series, empty state, storage warnings |
31: | `/series/new` | Create a saved series |
32: | `/series/:id` | Fetch and inspect observations, edit or delete |
33: | `/series/:id/edit` | Edit a saved series |
34: 
35: The app redirects `/` and unknown routes to `/series`.
36: 
37: ## Data
38: 
39: The app calls:
40: 
41: ```text
42: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_m
43: ```
44: 
45: It always sends `freq=M`, `s_adj=SA`, `age=TOTAL`, `unit=PC_ACT`, and `format=JSON`. The only
46: user-selectable dimensions are:
47: 
48: - `geo`: `PL`, `DE`, `FR`, `ES`, `IT`
49: - `sex`: `T`, `M`, `F`
50: 
51: The service validates the JSON-stat dataset, decodes flat value indexes, drops non-finite values,
52: sorts observations by period, and caches successful responses for five minutes. The detail page
53: shows the latest 24 observations by default and can reveal the full history.
54: 
55: ## Storage
56: 
57: Saved series use the browser `localStorage` key `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1` with this envelope:
58: 
59: ```json
60: { "version": 1, "items": [] }
61: ```
62: 
63: Records are validated on load; invalid items are ignored with a warning. Corrupt raw JSON is copied
64: to `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1.corrupt` before the app starts empty. Data never leaves the
65: browser except for the public Eurostat request.
66: 
67: ## Limitations
68: 
69: - No accounts, server sync, export, or cross-device storage.
70: - Depends on Eurostat API availability and browser CORS behavior.
71: - The chart is a compact SVG trend view, not a full statistical charting tool.
72: - The example intentionally does not use Zetaris or any private credentials.
73: 
74: ## Attribution
75: 
76: Source: [Eurostat, `une_rt_m`](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/une_rt_m/default/table)
77: (unemployment rate, monthly). Reuse is subject to the
78: [Eurostat copyright notice](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/about-us/policies/copyright). The
79: dataset's statistical data is not presented as CC BY 4.0; see the
80: [license and attribution dossier](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/license-and-attribution.md).
81: 
82: ## Structure
83: 
84: ```text
85: src/app/
86:   core/eurostat/       JSON-stat model, API client, tests
87:   core/series/         Saved-series model, labels, localStorage store, tests
88:   features/            List, form, and detail pages
89:   shared/rate-chart/   Standalone SVG line chart
90: ```

Zetaris connection

The app reads the Poland total unemployment series from the Zetaris eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table view. Add a Zetaris API key for this browser tab.

Back to saved series
@if (configured()) {
A Zetaris API key is saved for this tab. It is kept in sessionStorage and is not written to localStorage or source control.
} @else {
No Zetaris API key is configured. Series pages cannot load data until you add one.
}

Use /zetaris-api with npm start. The dev proxy forwards it to ZETARIS_REST_URL and avoids the Zetaris CORS restriction.

@if (form.controls.basePath.touched && form.controls.basePath.invalid) {

Enter a path beginning with / or an absolute http(s) URL.

}

Usually 1.

@if (form.controls.orgId.touched && form.controls.orgId.invalid) {

Enter the Zetaris organisation ID.

}

Leave blank when editing to keep the key already saved for this tab. The key is never committed.

@if (error(); as message) {
{{ message }}
} @if (message(); as message) {
{{ message }}
}
@if (configured()) { }

How the request works

The app sends SQL to Zetaris at /sql-editor/sqls/run with the API key in the Authorization header. It queries the series view for observations and the metadata view for the dataset label, source, and update timestamp.

  • The API key is held in memory and sessionStorage for this tab only.
  • Saved series remain in localStorage; they contain filters and notes, never the API key.
  • The dev proxy is required locally because Zetaris does not send CORS headers. A production deployment needs a same-origin reverse proxy.
  • This is a local demonstration, not a pattern for publishing a Zetaris key in a public app.

# Eurostat CRUD on Zetaris

A small Angular 22 example that saves Eurostat unemployment-rate notes in the browser and reads the
observations from the Zetaris `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table` view. It is a standalone, zoneless
application with no backend, accounts, or database.

Zetaris currently exposes only the **Poland, total sex** slice of `une_rt_m`. The app therefore
offers one country/sex combination. It does not call the public Eurostat API.

The verified dataset notes live in the repository dossier:
[`docs/data-sources/eurostat/`](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/README.md).

## Run locally

Requires Node.js 26 and npm 11. The repository root needs a `.env.local` with at least:

```text
ZETARIS_REST_URL=http://localhost:8888/api/v1.0
```

`ZETARIS_ORG_ID` defaults to `1`. The app does not read `.env.local` itself; the Angular dev proxy
reads only `ZETARIS_REST_URL`.

```bash
npm install
npm start
```

Open `http://localhost:4200/`, then open **Connection** and paste the Zetaris API key. The key is
held in `sessionStorage` for that tab; it is not written to `localStorage` or source control.

```bash
npm test -- --watch=false   # Vitest unit tests
npm run build               # production bundle in dist/
```

## Routes

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/series` | List saved series, empty state, storage warnings |
| `/series/new` | Create a saved series |
| `/series/:id` | Query Zetaris, inspect observations, edit or delete |
| `/series/:id/edit` | Edit a saved series |
| `/settings` | Save, test, or clear the Zetaris connection |

The app redirects `/` and unknown routes to `/series`.

## Data

The app sends SQL to Zetaris:

```text
POST /zetaris-api/sql-editor/sqls/run
```

It queries:

```sql
SELECT period, unemployment_rate_pct
FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table
ORDER BY period ASC;
```

and:

```sql
SELECT dataset_label, dataset_source, last_updated
FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table;
```

The service sends `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`, `X-Org-ID`, and a UUID `X-Request-ID`. It
validates rows, converts the rate to a number, drops malformed rows, sorts observations by period,
and caches successful responses for five minutes. The detail page shows the latest 24 observations
by default and can reveal the full 356-row history.

## Dev proxy and CORS

Zetaris does not send CORS headers, so a browser page on `localhost:4200` cannot call
`localhost:8888` directly. `proxy.conf.cjs` forwards `/zetaris-api` to the origin and base path in
`ZETARIS_REST_URL`, which makes the request same-origin from the browser's perspective.

This is a local-development arrangement. A production deployment needs a same-origin reverse proxy
in front of Zetaris. Do not publish a build that contains an API key, and do not treat this browser
key entry pattern as a production authentication design.

## Storage

Saved series use the browser `localStorage` key `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1` with this envelope:

```json
{ "version": 1, "items": [] }
```

Records are validated on load; invalid items are ignored with a warning. Corrupt raw JSON is copied
to `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1.corrupt` before the app starts empty. Saved series never contain
the Zetaris API key.

The Zetaris connection uses the `sessionStorage` key `eurostat-crud.zetaris-connection.v1`. It is
cleared when the tab closes and can be removed with **Disconnect**.

## Limitations

- Zetaris currently provides only Poland/total (`PL`, `T`).
- No accounts, server sync, export, or cross-device storage.
- The API key is visible to JavaScript in the page and to anyone with access to the browser tab.
- The dev proxy is required locally; direct cross-origin browser calls fail.
- The chart is a compact SVG trend view, not a full statistical charting tool.
- Data freshness is the Zetaris registration's current vintage, not a local cache guarantee.

## Attribution

Source: [Eurostat, `une_rt_m`](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/une_rt_m/default/table)
(unemployment rate, monthly), served through Zetaris. Reuse is subject to the
[Eurostat copyright notice](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice). The dataset's
statistical data is not presented as CC BY 4.0; see the
[license and attribution dossier](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/license-and-attribution.md).

## Structure

```text
src/app/
  core/series/         Saved-series model, labels, localStorage store, tests
  core/zetaris/        Connection store, Zetaris SQL client, tests
  features/            List, form, detail, and connection pages
  shared/rate-chart/   Standalone SVG line chart
proxy.conf.cjs         Same-origin dev proxy for the Zetaris REST API
```

## Browser example

[`examples/eurostat-crud`](../../../examples/eurostat-crud/README.md) reads the series and metadata
views through the Zetaris SQL REST endpoint (`POST /sql-editor/sqls/run`). Zetaris does not send
CORS headers, so the Angular development server proxies `/zetaris-api` to `ZETARIS_REST_URL`. The
app asks for the API key at runtime and keeps it in `sessionStorage`; it does not read the key from
source, `.env.local`, or `localStorage`. This is a local demonstration. A production deployment
needs a same-origin reverse proxy or a server-side BFF, and a public app must not ship a Zetaris key.

## Security

- The repository's SQL helpers read the key from `.env.local`. The example app accepts a runtime key
  in `sessionStorage` for local development only.
- Never commit or embed `ZETARIS_API_KEY` in source, a notebook, a screenshot, or a document.
- A production browser app needs a server-side credential boundary; do not expose a Zetaris key to
  public clients.
- The Eurostat endpoint itself needs no key.
- The REST table registration does not add authentication to Eurostat; it adds a Zetaris object that reads
  the public endpoint.

390:   XMLs or `.vscode/` shared settings) that establish the project structure,
391:   SDKs, or common tooling MUST be tracked and committed to ensure environment
392:   parity. Workspace-specific or personal settings (e.g., `workspace.xml`) MUST
393:   remain ignored.
394: - **Example**: If adding a new rule file introduces new technical terms, the
395:   cSpell update for those terms MUST be part of the same atomic unit as the
396:   rule file addition.
397: 
398: ***
399: 
400: ## 7. Phase 7: Submodule Synchronization Protocol
401: 
402: When managing submodules, the main repository's history must remain descriptive
403: and clear.
404: 
405: - **Synchronized Commits**: Every functional update in a submodule requiring a
406:   pointer update in the main repo MUST be coupled with its relevant main-repo
407:   configuration changes (e.g., CI scripts or IDE settings).
408: - **Orchestration**: Delegate metadata extraction to the
409:   `git_submodule_commit_details` skill to ensure zero-omission fidelity.
410: - **Commit Message Generation**: All submodule sync commits MUST follow the
411:   strict formatting, chronological ordering, and metadata requirements defined in
412:   [git-commit-message-rules.md#5-submodule-sync-commits-parent-repository](./git-commit-message-rules.md#5-submodule-sync-commits-parent-repository).
413: - **Submodule History Integrity**: Before updating a submodule pointer in the
414:   parent repository, the changes *within* the submodule MUST be committed
415:   according to these exact atomic construction rules. A "dirty" or
416:   uncommitted submodule state is prohibited during a parent-repo sync.
417: 
418: ***
419: 
420: ### 7.1 Ordering & Priority (CRITICAL)
421: 
422: - **Submodule-First Discipline**: When a submodule has pending commits (either
423:   staged, unstaged, or untracked), the agent MUST handle ALL submodule commits
424:   BEFORE proceeding to any parent-repository work. Submodule work takes
425:   absolute priority.
426: - **Parent Sync Trigger**: ONLY after the submodule's working tree is clean and
427:   all submodule commits are finalized does the agent check the parent repository
428:   for a stale submodule pointer. If the parent's recorded SHA differs from the
429:   submodule's HEAD, the parent sync commit becomes the **next atomic unit**.
430: 
431: ***
432: 
433: ### 7.2 Parent-Side Change Grouping
434: 
435: - **Related Parent Changes CAN be Grouped**: If the parent repository contains
436:   unstaged changes that are **directly related to the submodule update** (e.g.,
437:   adding skill implementation code for a newly committed rule, updating CI
438:   workflows that reference the submodule, or documentation that describes the
439:   submodule's new behavior), these changes MAY be combined with the submodule
440:   SHA sync commit into a single atomic unit.
441:     - The combined commit MUST clearly document BOTH the submodule pointer advance
442:     AND the parent-side functional changes in the commit body.
443:     - The commit message MUST explain the coupling rationale: e.g., "Skill
444:     implementation for the newly mandated rule" or "CI update to support
445:     submodule's new behavior."
446: - **Unrelated Parent Changes MUST be Separate**: If the parent repository has
447:   changes unrelated to the submodule update (e.g., fixing a typo in an unrelated
448:   README, updating a different skill), these MUST be staged and committed
449:   **after** the submodule sync commit completes, as a separate atomic unit.
450: 
451: ***
452: 
453: ### 7.3 Automatic Parent Sync Offer (MANDATORY)
454: 
455: Immediately after successfully committing ANY change to a submodule repository,
456: the agent MUST:
457: 
458: 1. **Check parent state** — If the submodule is nested inside a parent Git repo,
459:    run `git -C <parent-path> status` to verify the submodule entry shows
460:    `modified: <submodule-name> (new commits)`.
461: 2. **Present arranged commit preview** — Show the parent sync commit using the
462:    full arranged commits format (§4) BEFORE the user has a chance to say
463:    anything else.
464:    - If parent-side related changes exist, group them with the SHA update as
465:      described in §7.2.
466: 3. **Prompt explicitly**: "The parent repository needs a submodule SHA update.
467:    Execute sync?" (or equivalent directive).
468: 4. **On "yes"** — Execute the parent sync commit **immediately** without
469:    re-preview.
470: 5. **On "no" or ambiguous** — Do NOT commit. Await explicit user directive.
471: 6. **Do not proceed** to unrelated tasks until the parent sync matter is
472:    resolved (either committed or explicitly deferred by user).
473: 
474: ***
475: 
476: ## 8. Phase 8: Handling Generated Files vs. User Customization
477: 
478: When a file (e.g., `.gitignore`) contains both standard API-generated content
479: (e.g., from gitignore.io) and user-defined custom rules, these MUST be split
480: into separate commits.
481: 
482: - **Commit A (The Foundation)**: Commit **only** the standard, API-generated
483:   portion first.
484: - **Methodology**: Back up the full file, overwrite with the exact API content
485:   (or equivalent standard sections), and commit.
486: - **Rationale**: Establishes a clean, reproducible baseline.
487: - **Commit B (The Customization)**: Commit the user-defined sections (patches/
488:   custom rules) in a subsequent commit.
489: - **Rationale**: Clearly distinguishes between "standard boilerplate" and
490:   "project-specific logic".
491: - **Handling Modifications**: If the user has altered the API-generated
492:   portion, these alterations must also be separated from the raw API import
493:   if possible, or documented clearly as user-patches on top of the base.
494: 
495: ***
496: 
497: ## 9. Phase 9: Commit Message Quality Standards
498: 
499: - **Specificity Over Genericity**: Avoid generic titles like `os-specific`.
500:   Instead, list the specific components: `add linux, macos, and windows
501:   gitignore rules`.
502: - **Anti-Repetition**: The commit body MUST NOT merely rephrase the title.
503: - **Bad**: Title: `add vscode gitignore rules`. Body: `Add VisualStudioCode
504:   exclusion rules`.
505: - **Good**: Title: `add vscode gitignore rules`. Body: `Sourced from
506:   gitignore.io to exclude editor artifacts`.
507: - **Context Enrichment**: Ensure it explains the 'Why' behind the changes,
508:   especially for architectural or security-related decisions.
509: - **Reflecting Atomic Logic**: The commit body MUST explicitly state the
510:   rationale for grouping these specific changes together. If multiple files
511:   are involved, explain their functional coupling (e.g., "Updates both the
512:   API endpoint and the matching UI handler to ensure type safety for the new
513:   status field").
514: - **Constraint Documentation**: Mention any specific constraints or external
515:   dependencies that influenced the atomic grouping (e.g., "Includes the
516:   shared utility class to satisfy the compile-time dependency in the main
517:   logic").
518: - **Contextual Accuracy**: Ensure terms usage is precise (e.g., "Supabase
519:   project-specific" instead of generic "project-specific").
520: - **Body/Diff Congruence**: The commit message body **MUST** be a complete and
521:   accurate human-readable summary of all changes presented in the `Hunks/
522:   Preview` section of the commit plan. It is the AI's primary responsibility
523:   to make it easy for the user to confirm that the textual description
524:   perfectly matches the code modifications. Any discrepancy identified by the
525:   user requires an immediate and corrected preview.
526: 
527: ***
528: 
529: ## 10. Phase 10: Execution & Verification
530: 
531: - **Step-by-Step**: Execute commits one-by-one according to the approved
532:   arrangement.
533: - **Pre-Commit Sync Refresh (Mandatory before every commit)**: The Phase 1
534:   upstream check goes stale. After staging verification and BEFORE each
535:   `git commit`, run `git fetch origin` (non-mutating) and compare `HEAD`
536:   against `origin/<branch>`. If behind, STOP — do not commit; ask the user
537:   whether to `git pull --rebase` or merge (pull/rebase requires explicit
538:   approval per git-operation-rules.md), and commit only after sync. Repeat
539:   before EVERY commit in a sequence, not just the first.
540: - **History Refinement**: If existing commits need to be split or refined
541:   (e.g., to fix non-atomic changes), follow the **[Git History Refinement
542:   Rules](./git-history-refinement-rules.md)**.
543: - **Unstaged Changes During Rebase**: If rebase fails due to unstaged changes,
544:   use the stash workflow (see git-operation-rules.md Section 3).
545: - **Pull Before Push**: Always `git pull` (or `git pull --rebase` upon explicit
546:   approval) before pushing to incorporate latest remote changes.
547: - **Recovery**: If a mistake is made during staging, use `git reset <file>` to
548:   unstage, or `git checkout -p` to selectively discard. **WARNING**: Never
549:   use `git reset --hard` for synchronization; always prefer `git pull`.
550: - **Opaque Content Analysis**: For files flagged as binary or large assets
551:   (LFS), the agent MUST verify the internal consistency of the commit by
552:   inspecting the file contents (e.g., via `cat -v` or hex dump) to ensure the
553:   commit message accurately reflects the data being stored.
554: 
555: ***
556: 
557: ## 11. Phase 11: Logic-Documentation Alignment (Compass)
558: 
559: Imagine a compass where each cardinal direction is a logical area of the
560: codebase.
561: 
562: - **North**: Architectural/Schema changes.
563: - **East**: Logic/Feature implementation.
564: - **West**: Testing/Verification.
565: - **South**: Documentation/Refinement.
566: 
567: A high-quality commit history moves clearly through these directions without
568: "spinning" (mixing logic and documentation in one commit).
569: 
570: ***
571: 
572: ### 10.1 External Tool Asset Granularity (e.g., Postman)
573: 
574: When versioning assets for external tools (Postman, Insomnia, DBeaver), maximize
575: granularity by separating concerns:
576: 
577: - **Environments**: Changes to endpoints, variables, or credentials.
578: - **Collections**: Logical groupings of requests, tests, or scripts.
579: - **Data Tables**: CSV/JSON templates used for bulk-run or validation testing.
580: 
581: Never group these into a single generic `test(tooling)` commit if they serve
582: distinct purposes.
583: 
584: ***
585: 
586: ## 12. Phase 12: Source Logic & Generated Files
587: 
588: When working with repositories that use code generation, templates, or CI/CD
589: automation, the agent MUST distinguish between source logic and generated
590: output.
591: 
592: ### 11.1 Update the Source, Not the Output
593: 
594: - **Rule**: Never manually edit generated files. Always update the source logic
595:   (templates, scripts, CI/CD workflows) that produces them.
596: - **Examples**:
597:     - `README.md` generated from `templates/README.md.template` -> Edit the
598:     template, not `README.md`
599:     - `agent-rules.md` generated by `scripts/sync_rules.py` -> Edit the script
600:     or source metadata, not `agent-rules.md`
601:     - Build artifacts, compiled code, or auto-formatted files -> Edit source
602:     code or configuration
603: 
604: ***
605: 
606: ### 11.2 Identify Synchronization Mechanisms
607: 
608: Before making changes, the agent MUST:
609: 
610: 1. **Detect Generation**: Check for comments like `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED -->`,
611:   build scripts, or CI/CD workflows that regenerate files.
612: 2. **Locate Source**: Identify the template, script, or configuration that
613:   produces the generated file.
614: 3. **Document Sync**: Note in commit messages if manual synchronization is
615:   required (e.g., "Run `npm run build` to regenerate").
616: 
617: ***
618: 
619: ### 11.3 CI/CD Managed File Exclusion
620: 
621: Files managed by CI/CD automation MUST be excluded from manual edits during
622: history refinement or atomic commit construction.
623: 
624: - **Exclusion List**: Maintain an explicit list of CI/CD managed files (e.g.,
625:   `README.md`, `agent-rules.md`).
626: - **Grep Exclusions**: When verifying link updates, use `--exclude` flags for
627:   these files:
628: 
629:   ```bash
630:   grep -r "old-name.md" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude=README.md \
631:     --exclude=agent-rules.md
632:   ```
633: 
634: - **Commit Verification**: Before committing, run `git diff --cached` and verify
635:   no CI/CD managed files are staged unless the commit explicitly targets the
636:   source logic that generates them.
637: 
638: ***
639: 
640: ## 13. Phase 13: User-Requested Coupling & Deviations
641: 
642: The agent must strictly follow the atomic protocols defined above. However, if
643: the user explicitly requests to couple unrelated changes or deviate from the
644: rules, the following protocol applies:
645: 
646: - **Warn First**: If a request violates the Independence (Phase 2) or
647:     Configuration Coupling (Phase 5) rules, the agent MUST explicitly warn the
648:     user: "This coupling technically violates Rule [X] because [reason]."
649: - **Explicit Override**: The agent accepts the coupling ONLY if the user
650:     re-confirms or explicitly approves the deviation after the warning.
651: - **Documentation**: The deviation rationale MUST be documented in the commit
652:     message body (e.g., "Coupled with IDE updates per user request for atomic
653:     convenience").
654: 
655: ***
656: 
657: ## 13. Phase 13: Intermediate State Synthesis
658: 
659: When a file contains interleaved changes or massive structural reorders (e.g.,
660: 50+ lines moved) mixed with functional fixes, hunk-based staging
661: (`git add -p`) may become unreliable or impossible to isolate.
662: 
663: - **The Synthesis Strategy**: The agent SHOULD NOT rely solely on interactive
664:   staging for high-complexity overlaps. Instead, it MUST:
665:   1. **De-construct**: Manually edit the file (or use selective undo/revert)
666:     to match the current atomic goal BEFORE staging.
667:   2. **Stage & Commit**: Stage the "synthesized" intermediate version that
668:     contains ONLY the intended logical unit.
669:   3. **Iterate**: Repeat for the remaining changes until the working
670:     directory is clean.
671: - **Rationale**: Guarantees that even high-entropy working states can be
672:   refactored into a pristine, industrial-grade commit history.
673: 
674: ***
675: 
676: ## 14. Related Conversations & Traceability
677: 
678: - **API Refactoring & Postman Granularity**:
679:   [2026-02-11 Atomic Commit Refinement](./docs/conversations/2026-02-11-atomic-commit-refinement.md)
680: - **Rule Standardization**: [2026-02-11 Rule Refinement Session]
681: 
682: ***
683: 
684: ## 15. Phase 15: Guardrail Against "Predictive Planning"
685: 
686: The agent must never "commit" in a plan to what will be changed in the future.
687: Commit construction is a Real-Time Analysis task. The implementation plan serves
688: only as a roadmap for the **Protocol** of commitment, not the **Content** of the
689: commits themselves. Logic for commit construction must be synthesized from
690: Real-Time Analysis, never mocked in a plan.

If 864: the project *does* track them, coordinate with the team on which 865: metadata files are shared vs personal before discarding. 866: 867: #### 3h — Hunk-Stage Backup Cleanup (Sidecar Discipline) 868: 869: Every `git add -p` session, every in-editor `e` (edit-hunk) action, 870: and every programmatic `git apply` with a manually authored patch 871: may leave a sidecar file on disk: `.orig`, `.bak`, 872: `.full.bak`, `.rej`, `.staging-tmp`, etc. These 873: sidecars MUST be detected and disposed of before the commit lands, 874: never absorbed into it. 875: 876: Four-step protocol (Detect → Classify → Verify → Never-`add`): 877: 878: 1. **Detect** after each `git add -p` and after any `e`/`apply`: 879: 880: ```powershell 881: git status --short | Select-String -Pattern '\.(orig|bak|full\.bak|rej|staging-tmp)$' 882: ``` 883: 884: The output MUST be empty before the commit. 885: 886: 2. **Classify** every detected sidecar: 887: - **Recoverable** — content the agent or user still needs (e.g., a 888: `.rej` requiring manual re-application, or a `.full.bak` from 889: an aborted edit). Move it OUT of the working tree (e.g., to 890: `/../scratch/` or a personal-sandbox branch). 891: - **Disposable** — content already represented in the index, HEAD, 892: or another branch. Delete directly. 893: 894: 3. **Verify** before committing: re-run the §3h detect command and 895: confirm zero matches.     * Add a permissions guide covering how access works in Zetaris
    
    A single guide that summarizes the Zetaris Knowledge base on permissions and
    links to each page, plus the command reference for per-statement privileges.
    
    - How access works: what you can do (user types, roles) and what data you can
      see (object-level grants, row and column policies); deny by default
    - User types, users and roles, and the Management > Permissions page: a View and
      an Execute checkbox per resource (Data Catalog, Query Builder, Virtual Data
      Mart, Data Pipeline, Unified Semantic Layer, NDP File System)
    - Data object access (SELECT and INSERT grants) and row and column security
    - What each SQL statement needs, in the command reference's wording, with the
      vocabulary mapping View = Read and Execute = Write
    - How clients and applications connect over REST, JDBC and ODBC, including API
      keys under Management > API Tokens (up to three per user, shown once, with an
      expiry)
    - Least privilege for agents and applications: creating, updating and deleting
      is for administrators; reading is for ordinary users; each agent and app gets
      its own non-administrator user, granted through roles. Local installs and
      managed AWS clusters can both add users. Existing workflows are unchanged

1: # Eurostat CRUD on Zetaris
2: 
3: A small Angular 22 example that saves Eurostat unemployment-rate notes in the browser and reads the
4: observations from the Zetaris `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table` view. It is a standalone, zoneless
5: application with no backend, accounts, or database.
6: 
7: Zetaris currently exposes only the **Poland, total sex** slice of `une_rt_m`. The app therefore
8: offers one country/sex combination. It does not call the public Eurostat API.
9: 
10: The verified dataset notes live in the repository dossier:
11: [`docs/data-sources/eurostat/`](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/README.md).
12: 
13: ## Run locally
14: 
15: Requires Node.js 26 and npm 11. The repository root needs a `.env.local` with at least:
16: 
17: ```text
18: ZETARIS_REST_URL=http://localhost:8888/api/v1.0
19: ```
20: 
21: `ZETARIS_ORG_ID` defaults to `1`. The app does not read `.env.local` itself; the Angular dev proxy
22: reads only `ZETARIS_REST_URL`.
23: 
24: ```bash
25: npm install
26: npm start
27: ```
28: 
29: Open `http://localhost:4200/`, then open **Connection** and paste the Zetaris API key. The key is
30: held in `sessionStorage` for that tab; it is not written to `localStorage` or source control.
31: 
32: ```bash
33: npm test -- --watch=false   # Vitest unit tests
34: npm run build               # production bundle in dist/
35: ```
36: 
37: ## Routes
38: 
39: | Route | Purpose |
40: | --- | --- |
41: | `/series` | List saved series, empty state, storage warnings |
42: | `/series/new` | Create a saved series |
43: | `/series/:id` | Query Zetaris, inspect observations, edit or delete |
44: | `/series/:id/edit` | Edit a saved series |
45: | `/settings` | Save, test, or clear the Zetaris connection |
46: 
47: The app redirects `/` and unknown routes to `/series`.
48: 
49: ## Data
50: 
51: The app sends SQL to Zetaris:
52: 
53: ```text
54: POST /zetaris-api/sql-editor/sqls/run
55: ```
56: 
57: It queries:
58: 
59: ```sql
60: SELECT period, unemployment_rate_pct
61: FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table
62: ORDER BY period ASC;
63: ```
64: 
65: and:
66: 
67: ```sql
68: SELECT dataset_label, dataset_source, last_updated
69: FROM eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table;
70: ```
71: 
72: The service sends `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`, `X-Org-ID`, and a UUID `X-Request-ID`. It
73: validates rows, converts the rate to a number, drops malformed rows, sorts observations by period,
74: and caches successful responses for five minutes. The detail page shows the latest 24 observations
75: by default and can reveal the full 356-row history.
76: 
77: ## Dev proxy and CORS
78: 
79: Zetaris does not send CORS headers, so a browser page on `localhost:4200` cannot call
80: `localhost:8888` directly. `proxy.conf.cjs` forwards `/zetaris-api` to the origin and base path in
81: `ZETARIS_REST_URL`, which makes the request same-origin from the browser's perspective.
82: 
83: This is a local-development arrangement. A production deployment needs a same-origin reverse proxy
84: in front of Zetaris. Do not publish a build that contains an API key, and do not treat this browser
85: key entry pattern as a production authentication design.
86: 
87: ## Storage
88: 
89: Saved series use the browser `localStorage` key `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1` with this envelope:
90: 
91: ```json
92: { "version": 1, "items": [] }
93: ```
94: 
95: Records are validated on load; invalid items are ignored with a warning. Corrupt raw JSON is copied
96: to `eurostat-crud.saved-series.v1.corrupt` before the app starts empty. Saved series never contain
97: the Zetaris API key.
98: 
99: The Zetaris connection uses the `sessionStorage` key `eurostat-crud.zetaris-connection.v1`. It is
100: cleared when the tab closes and can be removed with **Disconnect**.
101: 
102: ## Limitations
103: 
104: - Zetaris currently provides only Poland/total (`PL`, `T`).
105: - No accounts, server sync, export, or cross-device storage.
106: - The API key is visible to JavaScript in the page and to anyone with access to the browser tab.
107: - The dev proxy is required locally; direct cross-origin browser calls fail.
108: - The chart is a compact SVG trend view, not a full statistical charting tool.
109: - Data freshness is the Zetaris registration's current vintage, not a local cache guarantee.
110: 
111: ## Attribution
112: 
113: Source: [Eurostat, `une_rt_m`](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/une_rt_m/default/table)
114: (unemployment rate, monthly), served through Zetaris. Reuse is subject to the
115: [Eurostat copyright notice](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/help/copyright-notice). The dataset's
116: statistical data is not presented as CC BY 4.0; see the
117: [license and attribution dossier](../../docs/data-sources/eurostat/license-and-attribution.md).
118: 
119: ## Structure
120: 
121: ```text
122: src/app/
123:   core/series/         Saved-series model, labels, localStorage store, tests
124:   core/zetaris/        Connection store, Zetaris SQL client, tests
125:   features/            List, form, detail, and connection pages
126:   shared/rate-chart/   Standalone SVG line chart
127: proxy.conf.cjs         Same-origin dev proxy for the Zetaris REST API
128: ```

1: # Eurostat unemployment data source
2: 
3: Verified reference for the Eurostat dataset `une_rt_m`, "Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data". The
4: source was last updated on **2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200** and was verified against the live API and the registered
5: Zetaris objects on **2026-10-23**.
6: 
7: This dossier is the detailed companion to the short catalog entry in
8: [`open_data/rest_apis/rest-api-sources.md`](../../../open_data/rest_apis/rest-api-sources.md) and the onboarding
9: scripts in [`open_data/rest_apis/sql/non_rate_limited/`](../../../open_data/rest_apis/sql/non_rate_limited/).
10: It records what the source contains, how to query it, how the Zetaris views decode it, what is missing, and how
11: the data may be reused.
12: 
13: ## What this dossier covers
14: 
15: - The statistical concept, dimensions, and full code inventory of `une_rt_m`.
16: - The exact public REST request and the JSON-stat 2.0 response shape.
17: - The registered Zetaris objects: one REST table and three views.
18: - Coverage, missing values, status flags, revision behaviour, and known source quirks.
19: - A repeatable verification and refresh runbook.
20: - The official Eurostat copyright and attribution rules.
21: 
22: ## Quick facts
23: 
24: | Item | Value |
25: | :--- | :--- |
26: | Dataset code | `une_rt_m` |
27: | Dataset title | Unemployment by sex and age - monthly data |
28: | Producer | Eurostat (`ESTAT`) |
29: | Frequency | Monthly (`freq=M`) |
30: | Unit | `PC_ACT` — percentage of population in the labour force |
31: | Adjustment | `SA` — seasonally adjusted, not calendar adjusted |
32: | Age class | `TOTAL` |
33: | Sex codes | `T`, `M`, `F` |
34: | Geography in Zetaris | Poland only (`PL`) |
35: | Geography in the full dataset | 2 aggregates and 36 countries (38 categories) |
36: | Time range, full dataset | `1983-01` to `2026-09` (525 months) |
37: | Time range, PL slice | `1997-01` to `2026-08` (356 populated months) |
38: | Observations, full dataset | 757,828 |
39: | Observations, PL slice | 356 |
40: | Data structure | `UNE_RT_M`, agency `ESTAT`, version `156.0` |
41: | JSON-stat version | `2.0` |
42: | DOI | `10.2908/UNE_RT_M` |
43: | Source timestamp | `2026-10-21T11:00:00+0200` |
44: | Zetaris database | `EUROSTAT_REST` (id 917) |
45: | Zetaris container | `eurostat` |
46: | Zetaris REST table | `EUROSTAT_REST.une_rt_m_pl` |
47: | Zetaris views | `une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table`, `une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table`, `une_rt_m_pl_series_table` |
48: | API access | Public, no key, no registration, CORS enabled |
49: | Licence | Reuse authorised with source acknowledgement; editorial content CC BY 4.0 |
50: 
51: ## Two ways to use this data
52: 
53: ### 1. Public REST API
54: 
55: The API is the canonical source and the only path that can return any country, sex, age, unit, or adjustment
56: combination without a new registration. It returns JSON-stat 2.0, a sparse, dynamic-key format rather than an
57: array of records. See [`api-reference.md`](api-reference.md) for the request contract and a decoder.
58: 
59: ### 2. Zetaris SQL
60: 
61: The registered objects expose one fixed slice: Poland, total sex, total age, percentage of the labour force,
62: seasonally adjusted, monthly. The `une_rt_m_pl_series_table` view decodes the sparse JSON-stat value object into
63: one row per published month. The metadata and snapshot views are low-risk helpers that avoid `explode()`.
64: 
65: The Zetaris objects are registered REST tables inside Zetaris, not a browser proxy. The public API remains
66: the canonical source for arbitrary slices; the SQL-facing story is the registered table and views. The
67: optional [`examples/eurostat-crud`](../../../examples/eurostat-crud/README.md) Angular app reads the PL/T
68: views through a same-origin development proxy because Zetaris does not send CORS headers. See
69: [`zetaris-integration.md`](zetaris-integration.md).
70: 
71: ## Documents
72:

103: ## Key findings and limits
104: 
105: - **2026-09 is present but empty for Poland.** The time axis ends at `2026-09`, but the PL slice's last
106:   populated month is `2026-08`. This is a normal reporting lag, not a gap.
107: - **The PL slice starts in 1997-01.** The 169 missing positions are the leading months from `1983-01` to
108:   `1996-12`, plus the empty `2026-09` position.
109: - **The Zetaris snapshot view is only three columns.** `une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table` contains
110:   `rate_1997_01`, `rate_2025_07`, and `rate_2026_07`. It is a spot check, not a wide-format table.
111: - **The 2026-09-19 onboarding scripts are a historical baseline.** The live source now has 356 values through
112:   `2026-08`; the script comments still describe 355 values through `2026-07`. The scripts are not edited by
113:   this dossier.
114: - **Zetaris exposes one slice only.** Other countries and sex codes require a new REST table registration or a
115:   direct API call.
116: - **Status flags are attached to observations.** Poland has two flagged months (`2009-01` break in series,
117:   `2009-12` definition differs). Italy has 109 flagged months in the total-sex slice.
118: - **Values can be revised.** Eurostat runs routine monthly revisions, an annual seasonal-adjustment review, and
119:   occasional major revisions. The dossier records the source timestamp rather than assuming immutability.

1: # Operations runbook
2: 
3: This runbook covers the Eurostat `une_rt_m` registration and the public API. It does not create, modify, or
4: delete anything unless a step explicitly says so. Run read-only checks first, and get approval before any
5: mutation.
6: 
7: ## Prerequisites
8: 
9: | Requirement | Why |
10: | :--- | :--- |
11: | Python 3.9 or later | Runs `scripts/preflight.py`, `scripts/run_sql.py`, and `scripts/onboard.py`. |
12: | `.env.local` | Holds `ZETARIS_REST_URL`, `ZETARIS_API_KEY`, `ZETARIS_USERNAME`, `ZETARIS_PASSWORD`, and `ZETARIS_USER_AGENT`. |
13: | Zetaris REST access | The registration and verification queries use the REST channel. |
14: | `curl` | Fetches the live JSON-stat response. |
15: | `python3` standard library | Parses JSON without extra packages. |
16: | Network access to `ec.europa.eu` | Required for live verification and refresh. |
17: 
18: No Node.js runtime is required for the data source or the Zetaris checks. The optional Angular example
19: needs Node.js 26; see [`examples/eurostat-crud/README.md`](../../../examples/eurostat-crud/README.md).
20: 
21: ## Preflight
22: 
23: Run this before any Zetaris work:
24: 
25: ```bash
26: cd /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started
27: python3 scripts/preflight.py
28: ```

30: Expected result:

33: [PASS] env file: /home/ext_root/lab-data/zetaris-getting-started/.env.local

41: READY

43: 
44: If preflight fails, stop and report the missing item. Do not create credentials or change the endpoint to work

223: Then create the same three views with `de` names. This is a live change and is not part of this dossier. For
224: ad-hoc analysis, the public API is simpler and avoids creating one table per country.
225: 
226: ## Browser example
227: 
228: [`examples/eurostat-crud`](../../../examples/eurostat-crud/README.md) reads the series and metadata
229: views through the Zetaris SQL REST endpoint (`POST /sql-editor/sqls/run`). Zetaris does not send
230: CORS headers, so the Angular development server proxies `/zetaris-api` to `ZETARIS_REST_URL`. The
231: app asks for the API key at runtime and keeps it in `sessionStorage`; it does not read the key from
232: source, `.env.local`, or `localStorage`. This is a local demonstration. A production deployment
233: needs a same-origin reverse proxy or a server-side BFF, and a public app must not ship a Zetaris key.
234: 
235: ## Security
236: 
237: - The repository's SQL helpers read the key from `.env.local`. The example app accepts a runtime key
238:   in `sessionStorage` for local development only.
239: - Never commit or embed `ZETARIS_API_KEY` in source, a notebook, a screenshot, or a document.
240: - A production browser app needs a server-side credential boundary; do not expose a Zetaris key to
241:   public clients.
242: - The Eurostat endpoint itself needs no key.
243: - The REST table registration does not add authentication to Eurostat; it adds a Zetaris object that reads
244:   the public endpoint.
245: 
246: ## Teardown
247: 
248: The create script comments out the teardown. If removal is explicitly approved, the views can be dropped with
249: SQL:
250: 
251: ```sql
252: DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_metadata_table;
253: DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_snapshot_table;
254: DROP VIEW eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table;
255: ```
256: 
257: The underlying REST table and Lightning database are removed through the Zetaris Data Explorer; the script
258: notes that there is no SQL path for those objects. Do not run teardown as part of routine verification.

(End of file - total 258 lines)
</content>

## 9. Phase 9: Commit Message Quality Standards

- **Specificity Over Genericity**: Avoid generic titles like `os-specific`.
  Instead, list the specific components: `add linux, macos, and windows
  gitignore rules`.
- **Anti-Repetition**: The commit body MUST NOT merely rephrase the title.
- **Bad**: Title: `add vscode gitignore rules`. Body: `Add VisualStudioCode
  exclusion rules`.
- **Good**: Title: `add vscode gitignore rules`. Body: `Sourced from
  gitignore.io to exclude editor artifacts`.
- **Context Enrichment**: Ensure it explains the 'Why' behind the changes,
  especially for architectural or security-related decisions.
- **Reflecting Atomic Logic**: The commit body MUST explicitly state the
  rationale for grouping these specific changes together. If multiple files
  are involved, explain their functional coupling (e.g., "Updates both the
  API endpoint and the matching UI handler to ensure type safety for the new
  status field").
- **Constraint Documentation**: Mention any specific constraints or external
  dependencies that influenced the atomic grouping (e.g., "Includes the
  shared utility class to satisfy the compile-time dependency in the main
  logic").
- **Contextual Accuracy**: Ensure terms usage is precise (e.g., "Supabase
  project-specific" instead of generic "project-specific").
- **Body/Diff Congruence**: The commit message body **MUST** be a complete and
  accurate human-readable summary of all changes presented in the `Hunks/
  Preview` section of the commit plan. It is the AI's primary responsibility
  to make it easy for the user to confirm that the textual description
  perfectly matches the code modifications. Any discrepancy identified by the
  user requires an immediate and corrected preview.

# Git Commit Message Generation Rules

This document outlines the strict rules for generating Git commit messages. These rules ensure history is readable,
automated tools can parse changes, and the intent of every change is clear.

***

## 1. Format Specification

- **Standard**: Follow the **Conventional Commits** specification.

- Format: `type(scope): description`

- Common Types: `feat`,`fix`,`docs`,`style`,`refactor`,`test`,`chore`.

- **Plain Text Only**: The final commit message must be **Plain Text**.

- **No Markdown**: Do not use bold (`**`), italics (`*`), or code blocks (`` ` ``).

- **Allowed Symbols**: You MAY use standard punctuation and symbols for clarity (e.g., `-`,`:`,`()`,`[]`).

***

### 2. Title Line (Header)

The first line is the most important part of the commit message.

- **Content**: A strong, concise summary of the *entire* change.

- **Context**: Include critical contextual information (e.g., dates for meetings, releases, or time-sensitive changes).

- **Length**:

- **Ideal**: < 50 characters.

- **Hard Limit**: 72 characters.

- **Case**: Use the **Imperative Mood** (e.g., "add feature" not "added feature" or "adds feature").

- **Punctuation**: Do not end the title line with a period.

- **Reference Style**: When referring to documentation sections, use the **Section Title** instead of the Section

    Number (e.g., use "Refine Migration, Verification & Secrets protocol" instead of "Update Section 9").

***

### 3. Body (Description)

The body provides the detailed context.

- **Separation**: There must be a **blank line** between the Title and the Body.

- **Structure**: Use **Bullet Points** (`-`) for all details. Do not use paragraphs of text.

- **Wrapping**: Wrap all lines at **72 characters**.

- **Content**:

- Focus on **What** changed and **Why**.

- Summarize the impact of the changes.

- **No Redundancy**: Do not repeat information already stated in the title. Provide supplementary details ONLY.

- **Meaningful Summaries**: Avoid exhaustive lists for repetitive changes (e.g., individual spell check words).

    Instead, provide a higher-level summary of the domain or impact (e.g., "Add 30+ project domain terms to workspace
    dictionary").

- **Self-Documenting Titles**: For standard style cleanups or simple deletions, the body MAY be omitted entirely if the

    title is exhaustive. Avoid adding "filler" or "gibberish" to satisfy a structure requirement.

***

### 4. Example

**Correct Format:**

```text
feat(auth): implement JWT token refresh strategy

Update the authentication flow to handle expired tokens automatically
without forcing a user logout.

- Add 'RefreshToken' service to handle token rotation.

- Update 'AuthInterceptor' to catch 401 errors.

- Add unit tests for token expiration scenarios.

- Update API documentation with new endpoint details.
```

**Incorrect Format:**

```text
Added new auth features

I added a new way to handle tokens so that users don't get logged out.
It uses a new service and I also updated the interceptor.
**Changes:**

* `RefreshToken` service

* Tests
```

### 5. Submodule Sync Commits (Parent Repository)

- **Title**: `chore(submodules): sync <submodule-name> with <descriptive-action>`
  - First line format: `chore(submodules): sync <submodule-name> with <action>`
  - Include a descriptive action that summarizes the changes
- **Short Summary**: `Updates <submodule-name> from <old-sha-short> to <new-sha-short> (<head-commit-title>)`
- **Full Metadata Body (MANDATORY)**: The body MUST contain the complete,
  structured industrial record of the submodule advance.
- **Changes Section Header**: `Changes (<submodule-name>) [<old-sha>..<new-sha>]:`
  - **Mandatory**: Use the full 40-character SHAs for both the previous pointer
    and the new pointer.
  - **Format**: Bullet points (`-`) listing commits in chronological order (older to newer)
- **Chronological Order**: The commit list MUST be ordered from **older to newer**.
- **Metadata Section Header**: `Metadata (<submodule-name>):`
- **Mandatory Fields**:
  - `Submodule: <name> -> <new-sha>`
  - `Submodule commit parent: <sha>`
    (merge: <parent1> <parent2> ← only if merge commit)
  - `Submodule commit msg: <title-line>`
  - `<body-paragraphs-if-multiline>`
  - `Submodule commit changes`: List paths and line counts (for the tip commit).
  - `Submodule commit author`: <name> <email>

# Skill: opencode-session-path-attribution

# OpenCode Session Path Attribution (v1)

## Composition Rationale

This skill is a **base primitive**: it owns ONLY the cross-session sweep
logic (session-dir discovery, newest-first ordering, turn-filename time
windows, token matching against stringified args) that the dangling-link
composer and ad-hoc "who did this" forensics reuse. It composes:

1. [`opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor/SKILL.md)
   — per-turn-file subprocess consumer of its stdout JSONL contract
   (SSOT for YAML parsing; never re-implemented here)
2. [`opencode-installed-plugin-lookup`](../opencode-installed-plugin-lookup/SKILL.md)
   — locates the logger plugin and its output convention
   (never the re-implemented locator)

The extractor answers "what did session S do"; this skill answers
"which session(s) did X, and when".

***

## 1. Environment & Dependencies

| Requirement | Minimum | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python | 3.12+ | `python3 --version` |
| extractor base skill | present | sibling script at repo root |
| logger YAML logs | `ses_<id>/NNN-<timestamp>.yaml` | `.opencode/logs/` |

Stdlib only. The extractor requires PyYAML — see its Environment section.

## 2. Operational Logic

### 2.1 Session & Turn Selection

- `--logs` default: **discovered** via Base #2 (`--plugin logger --json`),
  falling back to `<repo>/.opencode/logs`.
- All `ses_*` directories walked, **newest-mtime first**; `--session`
  restricts the set (each `ses_` prefix optional).
- Inside a session dir, turn files (`NNN-<timestamp>.yaml`) are processed in
  filename (chronological) order; `000-header-*` files are skipped.
- `--since` / `--until` windows are enforced on the **turn-filename
  timestamp** (`2026-08-07T04-14-05-689Z` → aware UTC datetime).

### 2.2 Matching

A record matches when **ALL** `--path` tokens appear (substring,
**case-sensitive**) in the record's stringified `args` (`json.dumps` of the
raw `args` dict — never a pretty-print or partial dict). `--tool` filters
are passed through to the extractor.

### 2.3 Output Record

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | str | session id, `ses_` prefix stripped |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC from the turn filename |
| `file` | str | turn file name (chronology-proof) |
| `tool` | str | tool name from the extractor record |
| `index` | int | extractor's per-session global call index |
| `args` | dict | raw args of the matched call (unchanged) |
| `match` | list[str] | the matched `--path` tokens |

stdout carries ONLY the payload (JSONL by default; `--json` = JSON array);
diagnostics go to stderr.

***

## 3. CLI Contract (Stable)

```bash
python3 scripts/attribute-path-to-session.py \
    [--logs <dir>] [--session <id>] ... \
    --path <token> ... [--tool <name>] ... \
    [--since <ISO>] [--until <ISO>] [--json] [--output <file>]
```

| Flag | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--logs` | No | logger logs dir; default = Base #2 discovery |
| `--session` | No | restrict sweep to this session id (repeatable) |
| `--path` | Yes | token that must appear in stringified args (repeatable) |
| `--tool` | No | filter turns to this tool (repeatable) |
| `--since` / `--until` | No | turn-filename time window (naive = UTC) |

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | at least one matching tool call found |
| 1 | no matches in the scanned calls |
| 2 | usage error, missing extractor, or logs dir absent |

Note the deliberate distinction: exit **2** for infrastructure problems —
callers must never mistake an uninstalled extractor for "no record".

> **Standard:** [Agent Skills (agentskills.io)](https://agentskills.io) ## Composition Rationale This skill is a **base primitive**: it owns the deterministic YAML-log → conversation-only-YAML extraction logic (layout discovery, multi-document round-trip parsing, field filtering, conditional agent retention, structure-preserving output). It is a **parallel base** to the existing all-fields YAML transcript extractor: both parse the same opencode logger-plugin YAML layouts independently, but they serve different contracts: | | all-fields JSONL extractor (parallel base) | this skill | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Output format | JSONL | YAML (structure-preserving) | | Fields kept | ALL (header, user, thinking, tool_call) | conversation-only (user.text, assistant.response, agent iff compaction) | | Library | PyYAML `safe_load` (structure-lossy) | ruamel.yaml round-trip (preserves comments, styles, ordering) | | Consumer | analysis composers (problem/solution/workflow) | archival / readable-transcript use cases | It was extracted as its own skill because the parallel all-fields extractor's contract (all-fields JSONL for machine analysis) is fundamentally incompatible with conversation-only structure-preserving YAML: the two need different libraries, different field rules, and different output shapes, and the parallel extractor already has a composer (`opencode-session-problem-solution-workflow-analysis`) that depends on its exact JSONL contract. *** ## 1. Environment & Dependencies | Requirement | Minimum | Verification | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Python | 3.11+ (3.12 recommended) | `python3 --version` | | ruamel.yaml | any | `python3 -c "import ruamel.yaml"` | ruamel.yaml (NOT PyYAML) is the only third-party dependency. PyYAML's `safe_load_all` is structure-lossy and cannot preserve comments, scalar styles, or key ordering — it is unsuitable for this skill's structure-preserving contract. The script imports `ruamel.yaml` and `ruamel.yaml.comments.CommentedMap` at module top; a missing package produces an exit-2 diagnostic — install it with `python3 -m pip install ruamel.yaml` or the system package manager before use. *** ## 2. Operational Logic ### 2.1 Input Layouts The opencode logger plugin writes two YAML layouts, both accepted by `--input`: | Layout | Path | Content | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Monolithic | `.opencode/logs/ses_.yaml` | Multi-document YAML (`---` separated): doc 1 = session header (`session:` key); docs 2..N = turns (`user:` / `assistant:`) | | Per-turn directory | `.opencode/logs/ses_/` | One file per turn: `000-header-*.yaml` + `NNN-.yaml`; filename order = chronological order | ### 2.2 Turn Schema ```yaml --- user: text: |- ... time: ... assistant: - agent: build model: {id: ..., provider: ...} thinking: |- tool_calls: - tool: write args: {filePath: ..., content: ...} result: |- time: ... response: |- duration: ... duration_ms: ... ``` A turn document carries BOTH the `user:` block and the `assistant:` block in the SAME YAML document. `assistant` and `tool_calls` are lists but may appear as a single dict — both shapes are normalized. ### 2.3 Field Rules (conversation-only) For each YAML document: 1. **Header document** (has `session:` key): pass through unchanged — keep `session` + `model` + `title` (structural identity: session id, creation timestamp, model, and title are useful archival metadata and are not user/response text). 2. **Turn document** (has `user:` and/or `assistant:`): - `user`: keep only `text`; drop `time`. - `assistant` (normalize list-or-dict to list): for each entry, build a new entry containing: - `agent` ONLY if `entry.get("agent") == "compaction"` (keep when compaction, drop when build) - `response` (the assistant's reply text) - ordering: `agent` (if present) BEFORE `response` - drop: `model`, `thinking`, `tool_calls`, `thinking_duration`, `thinking_duration_ms`, `time`, `duration`, `duration_ms` - **skip the entry entirely if it has no `response`** (entries that only produced tool calls with no textual reply are dropped) ### 2.4 Output Contract - **Per-turn dir input**: for each `NNN-.yaml`, write `>-transcript.yaml` into the output directory. Header file `000-header-*.yaml` → `000-header-*-transcript.yaml`. - **Monolithic file input**: write one `-transcript.yaml` (multi-document YAML, `---` separated) into the output directory. - Structure is preserved via ruamel.yaml round-trip: comments, scalar styles, key ordering, and `---` separators are retained. - **Derived artifacts**: every `*-transcript.yaml` file this skill writes is a DERIVED artifact. The source logs (`ses_/NNN-.yaml`) remain the durable SSOT. Readers holding only a transcript path who need the source files (e.g. for machine analysis via [`opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor/SKILL.md) or [`opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor/SKILL.md)) MUST resolve via [`opencode-session-transcript-to-source-resolve`](../opencode-session-transcript-to-source-resolve/SKILL.md). *** ## 3. CLI Contract (Stable) ```bash python3 scripts/extract-yaml-conversation.py --input \ [--output-dir ] ``` | Flag | Required | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `--input` | Yes | Monolithic `ses_.yaml` file OR per-turn `ses_/` directory of `NNN-*.yaml` files | | `--output-dir` | No | Output directory. Default: `/transcripts` (dir input) or `/transcripts` (file input) | ### Exit Codes | Code | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | | 0 | Success — at least one turn document processed | | 1 | No turn documents found (header-only input) | | 2 | Parse failure (YAML error) or missing ruamel.yaml | | 3 | Input path not found | ### Output Semantics - stdout: NOT used for payload — script writes files; brief diagnostics go to stderr only (`Written: `, `Found N file(s)...`, warnings). - ruamel.yaml round-trip settings: `typ="rt"`, `preserve_quotes=True`, `width=4096`, `indent(mapping=2, sequence=4, offset=2)`. *** ## 4. Scripts - [`scripts/extract-yaml-conversation.py`](scripts/extract-yaml-conversation.py) — Tier-1 Python CLI (stdlib + ruamel.yaml). Composition by Higher-Level Skills | Composer | Composition Mechanism | | :--- | :--- | | [`opencode-session-analysis-bundle`](../session/opencode-session-analysis-bundle/SKILL.md) | Calls `scripts/extract-yaml-conversation.py --input --output-dir /transcripts` at bundle Step 2; consumes the per-turn `*-transcript.yaml` adjacency as the archival transcript set. | Future composers (session conversation viewer, session archive, cross-session conversation diff) may consume this base. *** ## Related Skills | Skill | Relationship | | :--- | :--- | | [`opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor/SKILL.md) | Parallel base — emits all-fields JSONL (header, user, thinking, tool calls); preferred when the full narrative including thinking is required | | [`opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-tool-call-extractor/SKILL.md) | Parallel base — emits tool-call-only JSONL | | [`opencode-current-session-id`](../opencode-current-session-id/SKILL.md) | Sibling — resolves the current session's ID/title from the same logs | | [`opencode-session-transcript-to-source-resolve`](../opencode-session-transcript-to-source-resolve/SKILL.md) | Composer — resolves the transcript paths this skill produces back to the source logs (the reverse direction) | *** ## Changelog See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). *** ## Traceability See [TRACEABILITY.md](TRACEABILITY.md). 1: # Eurostat CRUD (Java)
2: 
3: A small Spring Boot web app that demonstrates the Zetaris Lightning JDBC
4: interface. It reads the Eurostat monthly unemployment series for Poland
5: directly over JDBC and keeps app-owned notes about individual observations
6: in memory.
7: 
8: ## What it demonstrates
9: 
10: - A Zetaris JDBC driver loaded through `SimpleDriverDataSource`.
11: - A `JdbcTemplate` reading `eurostat.une_rt_m_pl_series_table`.
12: - Read-only Eurostat data: the app never writes to Zetaris.
13: - Local CRUD for notes: create, read, update, delete, pin, rate, and tag.
14: - Thymeleaf server-rendered pages, no frontend build step.
15: - A health endpoint that checks `SELECT 1` against Zetaris.
16: 
17: ## Stack
18: 
19: - Java 21
20: - Spring Boot 4.1.2
21: - Maven
22: - Thymeleaf
23: - Zetaris Lightning JDBC driver `2.4.3.1`
24: 
25: ## Prerequisites
26: 
27: - JDK 21 or newer (`java -version`).
28: - Maven 3.9 or newer (`mvn -version`).
29: - Network access to the Zetaris Lightning endpoint.
30: - The Zetaris JDBC driver is vendored under `lib/`; no separate install step.
31: - `zip` and `unzip` on `PATH` only if you refresh the vendored driver.
32: 
33: ## JDBC driver
34: 
35: Maven first tries `com.zetaris:lightning-jdbc:2.4.3.1` from the configured
36: repositories. If it is not published there, Maven resolves it from the file
37: repository in `lib/`.
38: 
39: The vendored JAR is prepared from the Zetaris-supplied
40: `ndp-jdbc-driver-2.4.3.1-7eff043-driver.jar`. It removes the driver's bundled
41: Log4j 2, SLF4J, and Commons Logging classes so the app uses Spring Boot's
42: Logback. See `lib/README.md`.
43: 
44: To refresh `lib/` from a Zetaris-supplied JAR:
45: 
46: ```bash
47: ./scripts/install-zetaris-driver.sh /path/to/ndp-jdbc-driver-2.4.3.1-driver.jar
48: ```
49: 
50: Or set `ZETARIS_JDBC_JAR` and run the script without an argument:
51: 
52: ```bash
53: ZETARIS_JDBC_JAR=/path/to/ndp-jdbc-driver-2.4.3.1-driver.jar \
54:   ./scripts/install-zetaris-driver.sh
55: ```
56: 
57: ## Configure
58: 
59: The app reads three environment variables from `.env.local` in this directory,
60: which is gitignored. Start from the tracked template:
61: 
62: ```bash
63: cp .env.example .env.local
64: ```
65: 
66: Then fill in:
67: 
68: ```dotenv
69: ZETARIS_JDBC_URL=jdbc:zetaris:lightning@your-host:10000
70: ZETARIS_USERNAME=your-user
71: ZETARIS_PASSWORD=[REDACTED] ```
73: 
74: Do not commit `.env.local`. `run.sh` sources it automatically.
75: 
76: ## Run
77: 
78: ```bash
79: ./run.sh
80: ```
81: 
82: Then open:
83: 
84: - <http://127.0.0.1:8090/> — dashboard
85: - <http://127.0.0.1:8090/series> — Eurostat observations
86: - <http://127.0.0.1:8090/notes> — app notes
87: - <http://127.0.0.1:8090/health> — Zetaris health check
88: 
89: The server binds to `127.0.0.1:8090` only. It has no authentication and is
90: intended for local demonstration.
91: 
92: ## CRUD behavior
93: 
94: - **Create**: a note must reference an existing Eurostat period. One note per
95:   period.
96: - **Read**: notes appear on the dashboard, on the notes page, and on the
97:   matching series detail page.
98: - **Update**: edit the note text, tag, rating, or pinned flag. The period can
99:   change only to another existing Eurostat period with no note.
100: - **Delete**: removes the note from memory.
101: - **Seed data**: three notes are created at startup (`1997-01`, `2024-01`,
102:   `2025-07`). They disappear when the app stops.
103: 
104: ## Tests
105: 
106: ```bash
107: mvn test
108: ```
109: 
110: Runs unit and MockMvc tests. They do not need a live Zetaris endpoint.
111: 
112: ```bash
113: set -a
114: source .env.local
115: set +a
116: mvn verify
117: ```
118: 
119: `EurostatJdbcIT` is enabled only when `ZETARIS_JDBC_URL` is set. It reads the
120: real Eurostat table and checks `/health`.
121: 
122: ## Design notes
123: 
124: - Notes live in a `ConcurrentHashMap`; there is no H2 or JPA layer.
125: - The app uses one `DataSource` and one `JdbcTemplate`, both named for Zetaris.
126: - The Zetaris password is read from the environment and is never logged or
127:   committed.
128: - `spring.thymeleaf.cache=false` keeps template edits visible during local
129:   development.
130: 
131: ## Limitations
132: 
133: - Notes are not durable. Restarting the app resets them to the three seed
134:   notes.
135: - The app is a single-user local demo; there is no authentication or CSRF
136:   protection.
137: - The Eurostat table is read-only. Writes are deliberately out of scope.
